pages.title: The cash drawer and ledger
pages.summary: What More ▸ Cash drawer shows, the difference between the shift figures and the notes-and-coins ledger, what updates the ledger, and why it can drift.
pages.lead: The **Cash drawer** screen (More ▸ Cash drawer) keeps track of the cash in the till: which notes and coins are in the drawer right now, and the shift figures for the day. Every role can open it.

sections.basic:
### What the POS keeps track of
There are two separate records, and the screen shows both:
- **The shift:** the float you opened with, the cash taken in sales, money paid in and out, and the amount the drawer **should** hold. This is for checking the day at closing time.
- **The ledger:** how many of each note and coin the drawer **should** hold, with a history of what went in and out. This is what the POS uses to work out change.

Money is Australian: $100, $50, $20, $10 and $5 notes, and $2, $1, 50c, 20c, 10c and 5c coins.

### What you see on the screen
- **No drawer open on this register.** with **Open drawer with float**, when there is no shift. Otherwise a card with **Float**, **Cash sales** (*Net of cash refunds*), **Paid in**, **Paid out** and **Expected in drawer**, and the buttons **Paid in**, **Paid out** and **Count & close (Z-report)**.
- **Notes and coins in the drawer:** a row for every note and coin with how many the ledger holds (× 3) and what that comes to, and **Total in the drawer**.
- **Correct contents** and **Daily float report** buttons.
- **Cash history:** the 15 most recent entries, newest first. Each says what happened, who was signed in, when, which notes and coins, and the reason if one was given. Money that came out shows with a minus sign (for example **-$15.00**).

Opening, paid in and out, correcting and counting at closing are explained on [[cash/open-close]].

### What changes the ledger
You rarely have to touch the ledger, because most of it happens as you work:
- **A cash sale.** When you tap the notes and coins the customer hands over, they go into the ledger. When you confirm the change you gave, those come out. See [[pay/cash]].
- **A cash refund** that pays out cash: the notes and coins you hand over come out.
- **Cancelling a part-paid sale** that had cash in it puts the ledger back.
- **By hand:** opening the drawer, paid in, paid out, **Correct contents**, **Count & close**, and recording the daily banking from the float report.

### It works with the drawer closed
A cash sale updates the ledger whether or not a drawer is open. The shift figures, though, only count sales made **after** you opened the drawer, so open it at the start of the day.

### Each iPad has its own
The ledger and the shift live on the iPad you are using. Another iPad has its own, and they are not added together. They are also not in the backup file. If you use two registers, each one needs its own drawer opened and counted.

### Keeping it honest
The ledger is only as right as what is tapped. If you skip the tapping for a rush (the **don't track** buttons on the cash screen), or hand out different change than you confirmed, or take a note out for lunch without telling the POS, the ledger will drift away from the real drawer. Two things put it right:
- **Correct contents**, when you spot a mistake mid-shift.
- **Count & close**, which resets the ledger to exactly what you counted.

If **Can't make change** shows when you know you have the notes, the ledger has drifted. See [[pay/cash]].

### Other things on this screen
The [[cash/float-report|Daily float report]] works out which notes and coins to bank at the end of the day and the float to leave. **Check change** (a grid tile and a cart menu entry) tells you whether you can make change for a customer's notes before you take them: see [[cash/check-change]]. **Smart change** (Settings ▸ Payments, off until you turn it on) picks the change that keeps the drawer well stocked: see [[cash/smart-change]]. How the change itself is worked out, and what "Can't make change" means, is on [[cash/change]]. The cash-tender machine switch is greyed out and marked **Under Construction**; see [[cash/tender-machine]].
sections.deep:
### Why two records
The shift figures are plain sums of dollars: float, plus cash sales, plus paid in, minus paid out. They answer one question, "is the money all there?". The ledger is a count of each note and coin, and answers another, "what can I hand back as change?". They are kept apart on purpose. A sale where you skipped the tapping changes the first (the sale is still a sale) but not the ledger (the POS never saw the notes). That is why the closing count can show the right amount while the ledger was out of line, and why closing fixes the ledger without changing the day's figures.

### How Expected is worked out
**Expected in drawer** = Float + Cash sales + Paid in − Paid out.
- **Cash sales** only counts cash payments, from this register, made since you opened the drawer. Card and gift card payments are not counted.
- For a sale it adds what was applied to the bill **plus any cash rounding**, which is the cash the customer really paid net of change. It does **not** add the notes handed over, because the change went back out.
- For a refund it subtracts the cash that was paid back.

So a $13.02 sale paid with a $20 note, rounding on, adds $13.00 to Cash sales (the change of $7.00 is not in the figure at all).

### The numbers never go below zero
If the ledger did not know about a note and you take it out, the count stops at 0 rather than showing −1. The history entry still records exactly what you entered.

### What is kept
The history keeps the newest 1,000 entries and the screen shows the 15 newest. Entries made by a sale carry the sale's id and the person signed in. Opening, paid in, paid out and closing also add a line to the events history file (`events.csv`, in the app's `pos-data` folder, which shows in the Files app), which is never cleared automatically. **Correct contents** adds a ledger entry but no events line.

### Worked example
A customer owes $35.00 and hands over a $50 note. You tap the $50, the POS works out $15 change, and you give a $10 note and a $5 note. The ledger records two entries for the sale: **Cash received** (+$50.00) and **Change given** (-$15.00). Its total has gone up by $35.00, and so has **Cash sales** on the shift. If you had used **Exact amount (don't track notes)** instead, Cash sales would still go up by $35.00 but the ledger would not move.

### What writes to the ledger
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[takeCash in Pay.tsx] --> B[postCashSale: sale_in and sale_change]
  C[Cancel a part-paid sale] --> D[reverseCashTender]
  E[Cash refund change step] --> F[postCashRefund: refund_out]
  G[Drawer.tsx: open, paid in, paid out, correct, close] --> H[record then applyEntry]
  I[FloatReport.tsx: record the banking] --> J[paid_out entry then applyEntry]
  B --> L[pos.ledger]
  D --> L
  F --> L
  H --> L
  J --> L
  L --> M[planChange and planChangeSmart]
  L --> N[Check change]
  L --> O[Daily float report]
```

### Where the code is
| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| The screen, the shift, every sheet | `Drawer` in `src/screens/Drawer.tsx` |
| Cash taken since opening | `cashSince` in `src/screens/Drawer.tsx` |
| Ledger rules (counts, entries, never below zero) | `src/lib/cashLedger.ts`: `applyEntry`, `newEntry`, `cleanCounts`, `diffCounts`, `readLedger` |
| The notes and coins | `DENOMS` in `src/lib/cashLedger.ts` |
| History wording | `LEDGER_LABEL` in `src/lib/cashLedger.ts` |
| Writing sales, cancels and refunds | `postCashSale`, `reverseCashTender`, `postCashRefund` in `src/lib/cashSale.ts` |
| Banking from the float report | `FloatReportSheet` in `src/screens/FloatReport.tsx` |
| Where the data lives | `Shift` and `Pos` in `src/state/store.ts` (`pos.shift`, `pos.ledger`) |

### The ledger entry kinds
| Kind | History label | Written by |
|---|---|---|
| `open` | Opened drawer | Open drawer with float |
| `paid_in` | Paid in | Paid in |
| `paid_out` | Paid out | Paid out, and the float report's banking |
| `adjust` | Contents corrected | Correct contents |
| `close` | Counted at close | Count & close |
| `sale_in` | Cash received | A cash sale |
| `sale_change` | Change given | A cash sale, and cancelling a part-paid cash sale |
| `refund_out` | Cash refund given | A cash refund |

An entry's `delta` is what moved: positive for money that went in, negative for money that came out. `applyEntry` adds the delta to the counts, clamps each denomination at zero, and puts the entry at the front of `entries`, trimmed to `MAX_ENTRIES` (1,000).

### Saving
`patchPos` changes the in-memory state and saves the whole `pos` slice a moment later (a 400 ms delay that restarts on every change). On load, `readLedger` throws away anything it cannot read and starts with an empty ledger, so a damaged saved ledger shows an empty drawer rather than breaking the screen. The backup file holds settings and the grid only: it carries neither the shift nor the ledger.

### Reading the code for a fault
- **The drawer shows no notes but money is in it.** The ledger is empty: it was never opened or counted on this iPad, or the saved copy could not be read. Open the drawer or use **Correct contents**.
- **Expected is lower than it should be.** Cash sales only count from `shift.openedAt`. A sale made before the drawer was opened is not in it.
- **Expected looks too high after a refund.** A refund only subtracts cash tenders. A refund paid to the card does not.
- **The two iPads disagree.** They should: each has its own `pos.ledger` and `pos.shift`.
- **Tests.** `tests/cashledger.test.ts` (the tap pad, counts, applying entries, history cap, reading saved data, and the change finder), `tests/cashsale.test.ts` (writing sales, cancels and refunds to the ledger). The Expected sum and the Z-report text are written inside `Drawer` and have no test of their own.

pages.title: How change is worked out
pages.summary: Where the change comes from, how the notes and coins are picked, what "Can't make change" really means, and the three ways round it.
pages.lead: When a customer hands over more cash than is due, the POS works out which notes and coins to give back, using the drawer record. This page explains how it decides, and why it sometimes says it cannot.

sections.basic:
### What you will see
On the **Cash received** sheet, once you have tapped what the customer handed over, the line under **Due** says **Change to give: $…**. Tap **Next: give $… change** and the **Give change** screen shows **Take from the drawer** with the notes and coins to hand back. The buttons are explained on [[pay/cash]].

### The change is always exact
The POS only ever suggests change that adds up to exactly what is owed. It never suggests "close enough". If no mix of notes and coins makes the exact amount, it says so instead.

### Where the notes and coins come from
Two places, added together:
1. **The drawer record**, which is the notes and coins the POS believes are in the drawer (More ▸ Cash drawer). See [[cash]].
2. **What the customer just handed over.** Their own notes can go straight back.

Example: the bill is $7.00 and the customer hands over a $20 note, so $13.00 is owed. The record holds 1 × $20, 2 × $10, 3 × $5, 3 × $2 and 2 × $1. The POS suggests **1 × $10, 1 × $2, 1 × $1**: three pieces, the quickest to count out.

### Which notes and coins it picks
- **Normally:** the way that uses the **fewest pieces**.
- **With Smart change on** (Settings ▸ Payments): the way that leaves the drawer best stocked for the next sales, even if it is a piece or two more. See [[cash/smart-change]].

You can always hand back something different. Tap **I'll give different notes and coins** and tap what you really give. The total has to match the change owed before **Gave this** works.

### What "Can't make change" means
It means **no mix of the notes and coins the POS knows about adds up to exactly that amount**. It is about the mix, not the total.

Example: the record holds one $20 note. A customer hands over a $50 note for a $37.00 bill, so $13.00 is owed. The POS has a $20 and a $50 to work with. No combination of those makes $13.00, even though together they are worth $70.

It does **not** necessarily mean you have run out of cash, and it can be wrong, because the POS only knows what has been tapped. There are three possible reasons:
- You really do not have the right notes and coins.
- The record is out of date (a note went to the safe, or change was given without being tapped). Fix it with **Correct contents**. See [[cash/open-close]].
- The drawer was never opened or counted, so the record is empty. The box then says **No cash in the ledger**.

### What to do about it
The red box offers the ways round it, each explained with its buttons on [[pay/cash]]:
- **Ask for less:** take a smaller part of what they handed over and give the rest straight back.
- **Part in cash:** take some of the bill in cash and put the rest on card or another method.
- **Card:** take the full amount by card.

If you can see the drawer does have the change, tap **The drawer has it (ledger is out of date)**, then confirm the denominations you actually give (unless you choose not to track them). Put the record right afterwards. For the cashier steps, see [[fix/cant-make-change]].

You can also ask before taking the cash, with Check change. See [[cash/check-change]].

### Change on a cash refund
When a refund pays out cash, the **Give cash refund** sheet works the same way. The notes and coins come from the drawer record only, because nobody has handed anything over. The same buttons are there, including **Done, but don't track it**.
sections.deep:
### Why only exact change
The finder is asked for combinations that hit the amount with **no tolerance at all**. A drawer that cannot make $13.00 might be able to make $12.95 or $13.05, but handing back the wrong amount is never what you want, so those are not offered. The finder can look at near amounts (the float report uses that), but the change screens do not.

### Why the customer's notes count
If a customer hands you a $20, a $10 and a $5 for a $25.00 bill, a drawer with no small notes can still give the $10 straight back. Leaving their own notes out of the search would make the POS say "can't" when any cashier would simply hand them back.

### Fewest pieces
Of all the exact ways to make the change, the POS counts the pieces in each and takes the lowest. Fewer pieces is quicker to count out and quicker to check. If two ways tie, one of them is picked.

### A very full drawer
The search tries combinations one after another, and stops after 150,000 steps so a drawer with huge piles of coins cannot freeze the iPad. If it stops before finding any exact answer, it falls back to giving the largest notes and coins first, which almost always lands exactly. When that happens you see **The drawer holds a lot, so this is a good answer, not the only one.** In the very rare case where neither finds an answer, you get "can't make change" even though a combination might exist; use **The drawer has it** and tap what you give.

### How "Ask for less" is chosen
The POS looks at every part of what the customer handed over, keeping some and handing the rest back. It rejects any part that does not cover the bill, and any part whose change the drawer could not make. Of what is left it picks the **smallest amount kept**, and then the fewest pieces. Keeping everything is not an option, because that is the situation you started in. Example, with the record holding one $5 and a customer who hands over $20, $10 and $5 for $25.00: keep the $20 and $5 and hand the $10 back, so no change is needed. There is another example on [[pay/cash]].

### How "Part in cash" is chosen
Starting just under the bill and going down in 5c steps, the POS looks for the **largest cash amount** such that the leftover from what the customer handed over can be made out of the drawer plus their notes. The first one that works is offered, and the rest of the bill is left for another method. It needs the customer to have handed over more than the bill. Example: the record holds one $20, the customer hands over a $50 for $37.00. The $13.00 change is impossible, but taking $30.00 in cash works (the $20 comes back from the drawer), which leaves $7.00 for card.

### "Impossible" is only as good as the record
The record is a count of what was tapped. Every skipped tap (the **don't track** buttons) and every note moved without telling the POS makes it a little wrong, and a wrong record gives wrong answers in both directions: it can say "can't" when the drawer could, or suggest a note that is not there. That is why a count at closing, or **Correct contents** mid-shift, matters. See [[cash/open-close]].
sections.advanced:
### From owed change to the screen
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[CashSheet: cashStatus says change] --> B[pool is the drawer plus what was received]
  B --> C[planChange pool and owed]
  C --> D[findCombinationsLimited with delta 0]
  D --> E{exact answers found}
  E -->|yes| F[fewest pieces wins]
  E -->|cut short with none| G[greedyChange largest first]
  E -->|no| H[impossible]
  G -->|lands exactly| F
  G -->|does not| H
  H --> I[handBackOptions and partCashOption]
  F --> J[GiveCash: planChangeSmart picks the notes and coins shown]
  I --> J
```

### Where the code is
| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| The two steps of the cash sheet, the red box | `CashSheet` in `src/screens/CashSheet.tsx` |
| The change step (also used for cash refunds) | `GiveCash`, `GiveCashSheet` in `src/screens/CashSheet.tsx` |
| Due, short, exact, change | `cashDue`, `cashStatus` in `src/lib/cashSale.ts` |
| Exact change, fewest pieces | `planChange` in `src/lib/cashSale.ts` |
| The search itself | `findCombinationsLimited`, `findCombinations` in `src/lib/changeFinder.ts` |
| Largest-first fallback | `greedyChange` in `src/lib/cashSale.ts` |
| Ask for less | `handBackOptions` in `src/lib/cashSale.ts` |
| Part in cash | `partCashOption`, `reachableSums` in `src/lib/cashSale.ts` |
| Empty record check | `ledgerEmpty` in `src/lib/cashSale.ts` |
| Smart pick on the change step | `planChangeSmart` in `src/lib/changeScore.ts` |
| Where the drawer record lives | `Pos` in `src/state/store.ts` (`pos.ledger`); rules in `src/lib/cashLedger.ts` |

### The limits
| Limit | Value | What happens past it |
|---|---|---|
| Steps for one change search (`planChange`) | 150,000 | falls back to `greedyChange`, and `truncated` is true |
| Steps per search inside Ask for less | 20,000 | the search falls back to largest-first, and a part that still fails is skipped |
| Parts of the handover looked at by `handBackOptions` | 600 | it stops looking and uses the best so far |
| Sums remembered by `reachableSums` | 50,000 | it stops adding more |

`planChange` ignores any count that is zero or negative, so a drawer record with stray negatives cannot make a combination out of nothing. The finder's own tolerance argument is 500 cents by default, but `planChange` passes 0.

### Reading the code for a fault
- **The big button is greyed and the box says Can't make change, but the drawer has it.** The record is out of date. `planChange` only sees `pos.ledger.counts`. Use **The drawer has it**, then fix the record.
- **The box says No cash in the ledger.** `ledgerEmpty` is true: the record has no cash at all. It was never opened or counted on this iPad, or the saved copy could not be read. Open the drawer, or use **Correct contents**.
- **The suggestion includes a note the drawer does not have.** The record is too high. Someone used **Done, but don't track it**, or gave change without confirming.
- **No Ask for less option appears.** `handBackOptions` found no part of the handover that covers the bill and has makeable change, or hit its 600-parts limit when many different notes were handed over.
- **No Part in cash option appears.** `partCashOption` needs more handed over than the bill, and no 5c-step amount below the bill works, or one was already chosen.
- **The drawer holds a lot appears.** `truncated` is true: the search hit its step limit.
- **Tests.** `tests/cashsale.test.ts` (due, change, ask for less, part in cash, ledger entries), `tests/cashledger.test.ts` (the change finder, checked against your original function on random drawers).

pages.title: Check change
pages.summary: Ask the POS, before you take a customer's notes, whether the drawer can make the change for this sale, whether it is worth it, or whether to ask for card.
pages.lead: **Check change** answers one question before any money changes hands: *the customer says they have these notes. Can we give them change for this sale?* Nothing is recorded and the cart is not touched.

sections.basic:
### Opening it
There are three ways in:
- **A grid tile** called **Check change** (Edit grid ▸ Add tile ▸ Actions). A new grid has it already. A grid made before the tile existed does not, so add it. See [[sales/grid]].
- **The cart ••• menu**: **Check change**, with *Can we make change for this cart?* under it.
- **The guided checkout**: **More options** ▸ **Check change**.

### What you see
- At the top, **Cart total** and the amount. This is what is still owing on the sale, and when **Cash rounding (5c)** is on it is rounded to the nearest 5c, the same as the cash sheet would ask for.
- **Check a different amount** lets you key in any amount instead, and **Use the cart total** switches back. With an empty cart the keypad is already open under **Amount to check**.
- **What the customer says they have**, the same tap pad as the cash sheet. Tap each note and coin they say they have. **Customer has** shows the total. The pad has the **Add / Remove** switch, **Undo** and **Start over**, as on [[pay/cash]].
- Underneath, a coloured box with the answer.

Until you tap something it says *Tap their notes and coins to see what we can do.*

### The answers
| Colour and title | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Green: **Cash works: no change needed** | Part of what they hold pays the bill exactly | Ask for those notes and coins. The box also says what they keep. |
| Green: **Cash works: $… change** | They hand over a note or two and we can give the change | Ask for the notes and coins listed, and give the change listed. |
| Amber: **We can make $… change, but it may not be worth it** | We can, but it would leave the drawer thin | Card is the safer choice. The box says why. |
| Red: **We can't make the change** | No part of what they hold works | Ask for card, or take the part in cash the box suggests and put the rest on card. |
| Red: **They're $… short in cash** | What they hold is less than the bill | Ask for card, or take what they have as a part payment. |

### How it picks what to ask for
It looks at every part of what the customer says they have:
1. If some part pays the bill **exactly**, that wins, using the fewest notes and coins.
2. Otherwise it asks for the **smallest handover** that covers the bill and whose change we can make. That means they keep the most of their own money.

For example, a $37.00 bill, a drawer with plenty of change, and a customer with a $50 and a $20: it asks for the $50 and tells you the customer keeps the $20, because the $20 alone is not enough.

### Is it worth it?
The amber box appears when making the change would leave the drawer thin. With **Smart change** off, that means either:
- the change **uses up the last** of a note or coin of $20 or smaller (for example *uses up the last $10*), or
- the change **takes more than half** the cash in the drawer.

With **Smart change** on, the warning is based on what the next sales are likely to need instead. See [[cash/smart-change]].

Amber is advice, not a block. You can still take the cash.

### If the box says the ledger is empty
A red line says *The drawer ledger is empty, so this can't know what change you have.* The POS has no record of cash in the drawer, so it cannot say. Open the drawer or use **Correct contents** first. See [[cash/open-close]].

### Using the answer
Check change does not take any payment. When the customer agrees, go to **Charge** ▸ **Cash** and tap what they actually hand over, as normal. See [[pay/cash]].
sections.deep:
### Why it is separate from the cash sheet
The cash sheet works with what the customer **has already handed over**, and the change it works out comes from that whole handover. Check change works earlier, from what they **say they have**, and it considers handing over **only part** of it. That is how it can tell you to ask for the $50 and let them keep the $20, before they have handed anything over. (The cash sheet's **Ask for less** reaches a similar answer, but only after the notes are in your hand.) Both use the same change search. See [[cash/change]].

### How the best handover is ranked
Every part of what the customer holds that covers the bill is tried. Each one is ranked by three things, in order:
1. **Exact payment** beats everything.
2. **Less change** beats more change (so they keep more).
3. **Fewer pieces** breaks any tie.

Parts whose change the drawer cannot make are skipped. If nothing is left, the answer is "can't make the change".

### What the card answer suggests
When no part works, the POS also looks for **part in cash**: the biggest cash amount, in 5c steps, whose change can be made, with the rest on card. Example: the record holds one $20, a customer says they have a $50, and the bill is $37.00. The $13.00 change cannot be made, but $30.00 in cash can (the $20 comes back from the drawer), so the box says to take $30.00 in cash and put the other $7.00 on card.

### The short answer has no part-cash suggestion
If what they hold is less than the bill, the box says they are short and suggests card or a part payment, but does not work out a cash amount for you. You can simply take what they have as a part payment.

### Two meanings of "worth it"
Plain rules are used when Smart change is off, so the answer is something you can check by looking at the drawer. With it on, the answer comes from the learned profile, so it can warn about a note that is not yet *quite* gone but will be needed. Neither ever changes whether change can be made, only the advice. The line at the bottom of the sheet says which is in use and what it is based on.

### A very large handover
If the customer holds a great many notes and coins, the POS stops looking after trying 2,000 parts of the handover. It then answers from the best found so far, which could be "can't make the change" even though a part it never reached would have worked. In practice, ask a customer holding that much cash what they would like to hand over.
sections.advanced:
### From taps to a verdict
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[CheckChangeSheet: due and the tapped notes and coins] --> B[checkChange drawer offered due profile]
  B --> C{offered covers the bill}
  C -->|no| D[short]
  C -->|yes| E[try every part of offered up to 2000]
  E --> F{any part with makeable change}
  F -->|no| G[card plus partCashOption]
  F -->|exact payment| H[exact]
  F -->|needs change| I[change plus tight reasons]
  I --> J{profile usable}
  J -->|yes| K[planChangeSmart and smartTightness]
  J -->|no| L[planChange and tightness]
  D --> M[adviceFor writes the box]
  G --> M
  H --> M
  K --> M
  L --> M
```

### Where the code is
| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| The sheet | `CheckChangeSheet` in `src/screens/CheckChange.tsx` |
| The verdict | `checkChange` in `src/lib/checkChange.ts` |
| The words in the box | `adviceFor` in `src/lib/checkChange.ts` |
| The plain worth-it rule | `tightness` in `src/lib/checkChange.ts` |
| The learned worth-it rule | `smartTightness`, `profileNote` in `src/lib/changeScore.ts` |
| The cash due, with rounding | `cashDue` in `src/lib/cashSale.ts`; what remains comes from `usePriced` and `paidTotal` |
| The profile (null when Smart change is off) | `useCashProfile` in `src/state/cashProfile.ts` |
| The tap pad | `DenomPad` in `src/ui/DenomPad.tsx` |
| The grid tile | the `check_change` action in `src/lib/grid.ts`, handled in `src/screens/Checkout.tsx` |
| The cart menu and guided checkout entries | `src/screens/CartPane.tsx`, `src/screens/GuidedCheckout.tsx` |

### Result shapes
`checkChange` returns one of four:
- `short`: `shortBy`, and `part` which is always null.
- `exact`: `take` (what to ask for) and `handBack` (what they keep).
- `change`: `take`, `handBack`, `change` and `tight`, a list of reasons it may not be worth it. An empty list means no concerns.
- `card`: `part`, the part-cash option or null.

The amber or green tone is decided in `adviceFor`: a `change` result with any `tight` entries is amber.

### The plain worth-it rule
`tightness` looks at the drawer after taking the customer's notes in and giving the change out. It flags a denomination of $20 or smaller that is in the change and is at zero afterwards, and it flags change worth more than half of the drawer plus what was taken in. The smart version is `smartTightness`: it flags a coverage of less than half of usual change amounts, a drop of 15 percentage points or more, or a note or coin the profile expects to run short of.

### Reading the code for a fault
- **Nothing happens when I tap notes.** `due` is zero (empty cart) and no amount has been keyed in. Use **Check a different amount**.
- **The answer is always can't make the change.** The record is empty or out of date. The red ledger line is shown when `ledgerEmpty`. Use **Correct contents**.
- **The tile is missing from the grid.** The layout was made before `check_change` existed. Add it from Edit grid ▸ Add tile ▸ Actions. A register on an older app version drops the tile type from a synced layout, so update every register first.
- **The amber warning mentions usual sales.** Smart change is on, so `smartTightness` is in use.
- **The amount differs from the Cash sheet.** Check change always uses what remains on the whole sale (rounded with `cashDue` when **Cash rounding (5c)** is on). The cash sheet uses the amount of the payment being taken, so after **Split amount** the two differ. Use **Check a different amount**.
- **Tests.** `tests/checkchange.test.ts` (verdicts, ranking, part cash, worth-it rules), `tests/changescore.test.ts` (the smart rules).

pages.title: The daily float report
pages.summary: How to read the cash takings, recommended banking and float, and record notes and coins taken to the bank.
pages.lead: The **Daily float report** helps you decide what notes and coins to bank and what to leave in the drawer. It is a suggestion: count and handle the actual cash yourself.

sections.basic:
### Open the report
Go to **More ▸ Cash drawer** and tap **Daily float report**. If the drawer is open, the report covers the time since it was opened; otherwise it covers today.

### Read the figures
- **Cash takings** is cash sales minus cash refunds for the chosen period.
- **Take out (bank)** suggests notes and coins to remove. **Leave in the drawer as the float** shows what the ledger expects to remain.
- **Show another way** cycles through up to two other suggestions, when available.
- A warning may say the ledger and sales disagree. Count the drawer before banking if the count might be wrong.
- **Top up if you can** suggests notes and coins to add if the remaining float is below the recommended amount. Notes that are rarely used as change may be listed as better banked.

If the suggestion is right and you have physically taken the money out, tap **I took this out: record it**. Confirm the prompt. Do not record it before the cash has actually left the drawer. Tap **Close** to leave without changing the ledger.

### Where the cash history comes from
The report uses sales on this register and its own drawer ledger. It does not combine cash from other iPads. Cash sales or change you chose not to track can make the ledger differ from the sales total. Correct it or count and close the drawer if needed: [[cash/open-close]].
sections.deep:
### How it chooses what to bank
The report tries to take out an amount close to the period's cash takings while leaving notes and coins that are useful for future change. If it has enough history, it uses the same learned profile as [[cash/smart-change]], whether Smart change is switched on or off. With little or no usable history it takes the largest notes first.

The suggested float can be higher than the amount needed for today's takings. The report may suggest a top-up to move the remaining drawer towards its estimate. These are recommendations only; the cashier still takes out or adds the physical notes and coins.

### A banking entry changes the ledger
The report does not move money automatically. After you confirm that cash was removed, **I took this out: record it** writes a **Paid out** entry with the selected denominations. If you close the report or do not confirm, it makes no ledger change. It records at most the option currently shown, so do not press it twice for one physical banking.
sections.advanced:
### Calculation and ledger write
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Read this register ledger and cash sales] --> B[Choose period since open or today]
  B --> C[Recommend notes to bank and float to keep]
  C --> D{Cash physically removed}
  D -->|no| E[Close without changing ledger]
  D -->|yes| F[Confirm Paid out entry]
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Report sheet and confirmation | `FloatReportSheet` in `src/screens/FloatReport.tsx` |
| Period cash total | `cashSince` in `src/screens/Drawer.tsx` |
| Recommendation | `recommendFloat`, `ledgerTakings` in `src/lib/floatReport.ts` |
| Ledger entry | `newEntry`, `applyEntry` in `src/lib/cashLedger.ts` |
| Learned cash profile | `useCashProfile` in `src/state/cashProfile.ts` |
| Tests | `tests/floatreport.test.ts` |

`recommendFloat` limits the amount it recommends taking out to what the ledger says is present. With a usable profile, it compares candidate denomination combinations within $10 of takings and scores the drawer left behind; without a profile it uses largest notes first. The UI offers the best option and up to two alternatives. The cash report calculation is bounded, so an unusually large search can show that its result is good but not the only possible one.

### If the figures look wrong
- **The ledger saw a different amount from sales.** Some cash was not tracked or the ledger needs a count. Use **Count & close (Z-report)** or **Correct contents** before relying on the suggestion.
- **There is no amount to take out.** There may be no cash takings, or the ledger has no cash available to bank.
- **The report asks for a top-up.** It cannot add cash itself; take the displayed denominations from your safe or bank and add them by hand.
- **I took this out: record it** is missing. There is no positive amount in the suggested banking option to record.

### Known boundaries
The report is per register, uses the local ledger and local sales, and does not move cash or connect to hardware. Its profile is rebuilt from available local data; recommendations do not guarantee the next customer's change can be made. Always check the physical drawer.

pages.title: Opening, paid in and out, counting and closing
pages.summary: Opening the drawer with a float, recording money paid in and out, correcting the contents, and counting and closing at the end of the day (the Z-report).
pages.lead: This page covers the jobs on the **Cash drawer** screen (More ▸ Cash drawer): starting the day, recording money that goes in or out, fixing the record, and counting up at the end.

sections.basic:
### Opening the drawer
1. Go to More ▸ Cash drawer. If it says **No drawer open on this register.**, tap **Open drawer with float**.
2. The **Opening float** sheet opens. The line under the title says what the drawer held last time (*Carried over from last time: $…*), and the pad already shows those notes and coins.
3. Tap **Add** or **Remove** and the notes and coins until the pad matches what you are really putting in the drawer. The big number is your float.
4. Tap **Confirm**.

The screen now shows **Float**, **Cash sales**, **Paid in**, **Paid out** and **Expected in drawer**. Open the drawer at the start of the day: **Cash sales** only counts sales made after this point.

### The tap pad
The same pad is used everywhere on this screen. Tap a note or coin to add one. **Add / Remove** switches between putting money in and taking it off the entry. **×1**, **×5** and **×10** set how many one tap adds, which is handy for rolls of coins. **Undo** takes back your last tap and tells you what it removed and the new total. **Start over** clears the entry. Removing something you have not tapped says *None of that to remove.* The full description is in [[pay/cash]].

### Paid in and paid out
Use these for cash that goes in or out of the drawer outside a sale: a top-up from the safe, banking, paying a supplier.
1. Tap **Paid in** or **Paid out**.
2. Type a **Reason** (it helps when you look back at the history).
3. Tap the notes and coins that went in or came out.
4. Tap **Confirm**.

Both change **Expected in drawer**, and both are added to the cash history.

- If you tap **Confirm** with nothing entered you get **Nothing entered**. Tap the notes and coins first.
- If you take out more of a note or coin than the record says is there, you get **More than the drawer should hold**, for example *You are taking 2 × $20 (ledger has 1)*. It may just mean the record has not caught up with recent cash sales. Tap **Take out** if the drawer really has them, or cancel and check.

### Correcting the contents
If the notes and coins on screen do not match the drawer, tap **Correct contents**. The pad starts from what the record holds. Add or remove until it matches what is really in the drawer, add a reason if you like, and tap **Confirm**. It does not change the float, the Expected figure or the Z-report. It only fixes the record of which notes and coins are there, so the POS works out change from the right ones. You can do it whether or not a drawer is open.

### Counting and closing
At the end of the day:
1. Tap **Count & close (Z-report)**.
2. The **Count the drawer** sheet opens, with *Count everything in the drawer. Expected $….* The pad starts empty. Tap every note and coin that is in the drawer, including the float you are leaving.
3. Under the pad you see **Matches the expected amount.** in green, or **Over by $…** or **Short by $…** in amber. If it is out, recount before you go on.
4. Tap **Confirm**.

Confirm closes the drawer straight away and does not ask again, so be sure of your count first. Then:
- The iPad's share sheet opens with the **Z-report**, a short text summary. Send it to yourself by email or Messages, or save it to Files. **This is the only copy the app gives you**, so do it now.
- The drawer shows **No drawer open on this register.** again.
- The notes and coins you counted become what the record says is in the drawer, and the next opening starts from them.

### The Z-report
It lists the date and time, when the drawer was opened, and then:

| Line | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Float** | What you opened with |
| **Cash sales (net of refunds)** | Cash taken since opening, less cash refunds |
| **Paid in** / **Paid out** | The totals you recorded |
| **Expected** | Float + cash sales + paid in − paid out |
| **Counted** | What you counted |
| **Difference** | Counted minus Expected. A minus sign means short, no sign means over |
| **In the drawer** | The notes and coins you counted |

### Over or short?
Recount first, because a miscounted pile of coins is the usual cause. Then look at the Cash history for a paid in or paid out you forgot to record, and think about cash refunds and any sale where too much or too little change was handed back. A small difference now and then is normal. A difference that keeps coming back is worth a look at how change is being given.
sections.deep:
### Why opening starts from what is already there
When you close, the counted notes and coins become the record. The next morning's float is usually what is still in the drawer, so the pad starts there and you only adjust it. The float is the total of the pad when you confirm. A float of $0.00 is allowed.

If you tap **Confirm** without changing anything, you still get an **Opened drawer** line in the history, with nothing in it.

### Paid in and paid out and the record
A paid in adds those notes and coins to the record. A paid out takes them off, but the record never shows less than zero of anything, so taking out a note the record never knew about just leaves that count at 0. The history keeps what you entered.

The daily float report's **I took this out: record it** button records the banking in exactly the same way, as a **Paid out** with the note *Daily banking (float report)*. If a drawer is open it also adds it to the shift's paid out.

### Why Expected can be right while the record is wrong
**Expected** comes from sales and the paid in and out totals. The notes-and-coins record comes from what was tapped. Skipping the tapping on a cash sale (the **don't track** buttons) leaves **Expected** right, because the sale is still counted, but leaves the record out of line. So the closing count can match even when the record had drifted. Counting at close puts the record right, and **Correct contents** does it earlier.

### What the Z-report is, and is not
The text is made when you confirm and is only shown in the share sheet. The app keeps no copy of the text. What it does keep is one line in the events history file (`events.csv`) saying the drawer closed, who was signed in, and the counted amount, with a message holding the expected amount and the difference (both in cents) and the notes and coins counted. Opening, paid in and paid out add events lines too, and paid in and paid out include the reason you typed. **Correct contents** does not.

### Closing by mistake
There is no way to undo a close. If you closed early, open the drawer again: it carries the counted notes and coins forward, but it is a new shift, and **Cash sales** counts only from the new opening. The day's figures are then split across two Z-reports.

### Worked example
You open with a $200.00 float. During the day the cash sales come to $350.00 (net of refunds, with rounding included). You bank $300.00 with a **Paid out**. **Expected** is $200.00 + $350.00 − $300.00 = **$250.00**. You count $245.00 in the drawer, so the sheet says **Short by $5.00** and the Z-report says **Difference -$5.00**. After you confirm, the record says $245.00 is in the drawer, in exactly the notes and coins you tapped.
sections.advanced:
### What Confirm does
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Confirm in the sheet] --> B{which sheet}
  B -->|open| C[record open then the shift opens with the pad total as float]
  B -->|in| D[record paid_in and add to paidInCents]
  B -->|out| E{more than the ledger holds}
  E -->|yes| F[confirm dialog Take out]
  E -->|no| G[record paid_out and add to paidOutCents]
  F --> G
  B -->|fix| H[record adjust with the difference]
  B -->|close| I[build the Z-report text and events line]
  I --> J[record close so the ledger equals the count]
  J --> K[shift reset then the Share sheet opens]
```

### Where the code is
| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| The screen and `submit` for every sheet | `Drawer` in `src/screens/Drawer.tsx` |
| Cash since the drawer opened | `cashSince` in `src/screens/Drawer.tsx` |
| The tap pad | `DenomPad` in `src/ui/DenomPad.tsx`; `tapDenom`, `undoLast`, `describeTap`, `draftCounts` in `src/lib/cashLedger.ts` |
| Changes to the record | `newEntry`, `applyEntry`, `diffCounts`, `shortfall`, `summariseCounts` in `src/lib/cashLedger.ts` |
| The events lines | `csv.event` in `src/lib/csvStore.ts`; kinds `shift_open`, `shift_close`, `paid_in`, `paid_out` in `src/lib/csvFormat.ts` |
| The shift | the `Shift` type in `src/state/store.ts`, saved as `pos.shift` |

### How each sheet works out its entry
The pad's starting point (`base`) is the ledger's counts for **Opening float** and **Correct drawer contents**, and empty for **Paid in**, **Paid out** and **Count the drawer**. `submit` then turns the pad into a change to the record:
- **Open** and **Correct** record `diffCounts(entered, ledger.counts)`, the difference between what is on the pad and what the ledger held. Opening also sets the shift (`open`, `openedAt`, `floatCents` = the pad total, paid in and out at 0, the staff name) and writes a `shift_open` event.
- **Paid in** records the entered counts and adds the total to `paidInCents`. **Paid out** records the same counts as negatives and adds the total to `paidOutCents`, after the `shortfall` check against the ledger. Both write an event with the reason.
- **Close** records `diffCounts(entered, ledger.counts)` as `close`, so afterwards the ledger holds exactly the counted notes and coins, then resets the shift to closed with all totals at 0, writes `shift_close`, and opens the share sheet.

Expected is `floatCents + cash + paidInCents - paidOutCents`, with `cash` from `cashSince(shift.openedAt, registerId, sales)`: cash tenders on this register's sales from this iPad since the drawer opened, a sale adding amount plus rounding and a refund subtracting its amount. Difference is counted minus expected.

### Reading the code for a fault
- **Expected is wrong by exactly one sale.** That sale is before `openedAt`, from another register, or paid by card or gift card. Only cash tenders on this register count.
- **The Opening float pad is empty.** The ledger was empty. It was never opened or counted on this iPad, or the saved copy could not be read.
- **You closed but cannot find the Z-report.** The share sheet was dismissed, and the text is not stored. The shift resets as soon as you confirm, whatever happens to the share sheet. The events line still has the counted amount, and the expected amount and difference in cents.
- **Tests.** `tests/cashledger.test.ts` covers the pad, applying entries, the history cap and reading saved data. The shift sums (Expected, Difference) and the Z-report text are written inside `Drawer` and have no test of their own.

### Known gaps
Close has no confirmation step, and the Z-report is not saved in the app. Both are noted rather than changed here.

pages.title: Smart change
pages.summary: The setting that picks the notes and coins for change so the drawer stays stocked for the next sales, what it learns from, and how to read its reasons.
pages.lead: **Smart change** chooses which notes and coins to give as change so the drawer is still well stocked for the next customers, instead of just using the fewest pieces. It is off until you turn it on.

sections.basic:
### Turning it on
Settings ▸ Payments ▸ **Smart change**. It applies to **this iPad only**, like the drawer record it learns from. A line under the switch says what it is currently based on.

With it off, nothing changes: change is the fewest pieces, and Check change uses its plain "worth it?" rules.

### What you will notice
- **On the Give change screen** (cash sales and cash refunds), under **Take from the drawer**, a line says why that choice was made. For example: *1 more piece to count, but keeps 1 more $5 and 1 more $1 in the drawer for upcoming change.* If the quickest way is also the best, it says *Quickest way, and it keeps the drawer well stocked.*
- **Show another way** steps through the next best choices. The button then reads **Show the next way**, and finally **Back to the suggested way**. While you are on another choice the line says *Another way to make the same change.*
- **In Check change**, the amber "may not be worth it" warning is based on what your next sales are likely to need. See [[cash/check-change]].

You can always ignore the suggestion and tap what you really give. See [[cash/change]].
The [[cash/float-report|Daily float report]] also uses the learned profile to choose what to bank and what float to leave, even when this switch is off.

### What it never does
It **never** decides whether change can be made. If exact change is possible without Smart change, it is possible with it, and the other way round. It only chooses between the ways that are already exact.

### What the line under the switch says
| Line | What it means |
|---|---|
| *no history or item prices to learn from yet, so it picks the fewest pieces* | Nothing to go on. It behaves as if it were off. |
| *No tracked cash sales yet, so it is guessing from your item prices.* | It assumes customers pay a bill with the next note up, and works out the change from your item library. |
| *learned from your recent cash sales (about N counted, newest weigh most)* | It has real sales to learn from. |
| *learned from about N recent cash sales plus your item prices* | A mix of both, and real sales take over as they build up. |

### Helping it learn
It learns only from sales where you **tapped what the customer handed over and confirmed the change** (**Gave this**). The sales you skip with the **don't track** buttons teach it nothing about change. Give it a few days of tracked sales. See [[pay/cash]].

### When a suggestion feels wrong
Tap **Show another way**, or tap **I'll give different notes and coins**. Smart change is advice. If it keeps suggesting something you dislike, turn it off in Settings ▸ Payments.
sections.deep:
### What it is, and is not
It is a small statistical model that reads your own sales history, not a neural network or anything that phones home. Every number comes from the drawer record and the item library on this iPad, and the scoring is a short sum you can read below.

### What it learns from
Each time, the POS rebuilds a **profile** from three things:
1. **The drawer history.** Which change amounts you actually give ($8.00, $13.00…), how many of each note and coin that used, and what customers actually hand over. Newer sales count more: a sale 14 days old counts half as much as one today.
2. **The item library.** A customer buying a $12 item usually pays with a $20, so $8.00 back is likely. This is used while there are few real sales, and its weight fades as real sales build up, reaching equal weight at about 8 recent sales.
3. **The sales list.** Used only to size how far ahead to plan: about half an average cash-sale day (counting the last 28 days), kept between 4 and 12 sales, or 6 when there is nothing to go on.

Only sales you tracked count. Cancelled sales, cash refunds and untracked change are ignored when learning what change you give. Cash that customers hand over does count even if the change was not tracked.

### How a choice is scored
For every exact way of making the change, the POS imagines the drawer **after** giving it, and gives that a score. Higher is better:

**100 × coverage − 40 × depth − 0.5 × pieces**

- **Coverage** is the share of your usual change amounts that the drawer could still make exactly. 100% means you could still make all of them.
- **Depth** is how far each note and coin is below what the next few sales are expected to use. 0 is well stocked and 1 is out. Notes and coins used more often count more. Half of what customers usually hand over is counted as on hand, because it can be given back again.
- **Pieces** is a small push towards fewer pieces, so it only decides near-ties.

The best-scoring way is shown, and the next three are kept for **Show another way**.

### A worked example
Suppose your library has one item, at $12.00, and no sales have been tracked yet. The profile guesses that $8.00 of change is the most common (70%), followed by $38.00 (30%).

The drawer record holds 10 × $1, 10 × $2, 2 × $5, 3 × $10 and 2 × $20, and $8.00 is owed.

| Way | Pieces | Score |
|---|---|---|
| 1 × $5, 1 × $2, 1 × $1 (fewest pieces) | 3 | about 89.2 |
| 4 × $2 | 4 | about 90.6 |

Both keep full coverage, so it comes down to depth. The first uses one of only two $5 notes, and the profile expects $5 notes to be needed. So Smart change suggests 4 × $2 and says *1 more piece to count, but keeps 1 more $5 and 1 more $1 in the drawer for upcoming change.* The runner-up choices, 3 × $2 + 2 × $1, 2 × $2 + 4 × $1 and the $5 way, follow behind.

The weights are chosen to put stock first and speed second. They are a short list in the code if you ever want to tune them.

### When history is thin
Until there are sales to learn from, the guess is rough: it assumes bills are paid with the next note up. Real sales then pull it towards how your customers really pay, so it improves on its own. If you take little cash, it plans for fewer upcoming sales (as few as 4), so the suggestions stay close to the plain way.

### The learned profile is per iPad
The profile is built from this iPad's own ledger, so each register learns from its own sales. Nothing is shared between registers. See [[cash]].
sections.advanced:
### From history to a suggestion
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[useCashProfile in cashProfile.ts] --> B{Smart change on}
  B -->|no| C[null so planChange is used]
  B -->|yes| D[buildProfile from ledger entries and item prices]
  D --> E[CashProfile: amounts needPerSale inPerSale horizon confidence]
  E --> F[planChangeSmart pool owed profile]
  F --> G[planChange first: is exact change possible]
  G -->|no| H[return impossible unchanged]
  G -->|yes| I[findCombinationsLimited collects every exact way]
  I --> J[scoreAfter for the fewest 400]
  J --> K[best plus 3 alternatives plus explainChoice]
```

### Where the code is
| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| The switch and the note under it | `Settings` ▸ Payments in `src/screens/Settings.tsx` (`SmartChangeNote`) |
| Building the profile for this iPad | `useCashProfile` in `src/state/cashProfile.ts` |
| History and prices into a profile | `buildProfile`, `fromLedger`, `fromPrices`, `horizonFrom` in `src/lib/changeScore.ts` |
| The score | `scoreAfter`, `coverage`, `depth`, `SCORE_WEIGHTS` in `src/lib/changeScore.ts` |
| The suggestion and the reason line | `planChangeSmart`, `explainChoice` in `src/lib/changeScore.ts` |
| The warning in Check change | `smartTightness`, `lowOn` in `src/lib/changeScore.ts` |
| The line under the switch | `profileNote` in `src/lib/changeScore.ts` |
| The Give change screen and Show another way | `GiveCash` in `src/screens/CashSheet.tsx` |

### The numbers
| Name | Value | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `SCORE_WEIGHTS` | coverage 100, depth 40, piece 0.5 | the weights in the score |
| Half-life | 14 days | a sale this old counts half |
| Confidence point | 8 recent change sales | history and the item-price guess count equally |
| Horizon | 4 to 12, default 6 | how many upcoming sales to plan for |
| Amounts kept | 60 | the most usual change amounts in a profile |
| Candidates scored | 400 | the fewest-piece ways examined |
| Alternatives kept | 3 | for Show another way |
| Prior notes | $5, $10, $20, $50, $100 | which notes a customer is assumed to pay with |
| Prior change from | $20 and smaller | note and coin sizes the guess builds change from |

### What counts as history
`fromLedger` only reads entries that carry a sale id. A `sale_change` entry counts as a change given if all its amounts are negative and its note does not start with *Sale cancelled*. A `sale_in` entry counts towards what customers hand over. Other kinds (`refund_out`, `paid_out`, `adjust` and so on) are skipped. The ledger keeps only the newest 1,000 entries, so very old sales fall out anyway.

### Falling back to the plain answer
`planChangeSmart` always runs `planChange` first and returns its answer if it is not exact, so the plain and smart paths can never disagree on whether change can be made. If the profile is unusable (no amounts), or the exhaustive search is cut short before finding anything, it returns the plain answer with `smart: false`.

### Reading the code for a fault
- **Show another way is missing.** Smart change is off, or there is only one exact way, or the search was cut short.
- **The reason line is missing.** `smart` is false: the profile has no amounts yet, so the plain answer is shown.
- **It keeps suggesting a large number of pieces.** The profile says those coins are needed. Check the line under the switch for the source, and the Cash history for the sales it learned from.
- **Suggestions do not change after many sales.** Only tracked sales count. If most sales use the **don't track** buttons, `fromLedger` sees almost nothing.
- **Two iPads suggest different things.** They should: each builds its own profile from its own ledger.
- **Tests.** `tests/changescore.test.ts` covers the profile, the score, 60 random drawers where the smart plan is exact exactly when the plain one is, and a mutation check that the stock-keeping test fails without the depth weight. `tests/checkchange.test.ts` covers the worth-it rules.

pages.title: The cash tender machine
pages.summary: What the Under Construction payment setting means and how cash handling works until a machine is built.
pages.lead: The cash tender machine is a future connection point, not a working feature. The POS does not connect to a Raspberry Pi or automatically count or dispense cash.

sections.basic:
### What to do today
Use the cash screen as normal. Tap the notes and coins the customer gives you, then check the suggested change or tap the denominations you actually hand back. Confirm the cash by hand. For cash refunds, the POS can suggest what to give, but you still take the notes and coins from the drawer yourself. See [[pay/cash]] and [[cash/change]].

### The setting
Settings ▸ Payments shows the cash-tender-machine option as **Under Construction** and locked off. You cannot turn it on. Cash sales, refunds and the drawer ledger continue to work manually.
sections.deep:
### Why it is not available
The hardware does not exist yet. The current app deliberately has no connection, pairing, socket, or machine control. The switch is not a way to enable a partial integration.

### What remains manual
The cashier enters the cash received, checks or enters the cash to give back, and confirms the physical handover. The ledger changes from those confirmed entries. Do not assume a machine counted or dispensed anything.
sections.advanced:
### Current implementation
`TENDER_MACHINE_READY` in `src/lib/tenderMachine.ts` is `false`. The exported `tenderMachine` function is intentionally empty, and no screen calls it. The switch is therefore locked off. The request type describes a future accept/dispense operation; it is not an active API.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Cashier enters notes and coins] --> B[POS suggests or checks change]
  B --> C[Cashier handles cash by hand]
  C --> D[Cashier confirms the handover]
  D --> E[POS updates the drawer ledger]
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Locked feature flag | `TENDER_MACHINE_READY` in `src/lib/tenderMachine.ts` |
| Empty future port | `tenderMachine` in `src/lib/tenderMachine.ts` |
| Manual cash and change flow | `CashSheet` and `GiveCash` in `src/screens/CashSheet.tsx` |

pages.title: How the POS works
pages.summary: A short map of the register: local sales, Shopify sync, staff access and money rules.
pages.lead: The register is an iPad app that works with a Shopify store, a selected location, staff accounts and optional payment hardware. These guides explain the shared rules behind the screens.

sections.basic:
### Choose a topic
- Where sales and settings live, and how Shopify sync works: [[concepts/data-and-sync]].
- What staff roles mean and who can use or change settings: [[concepts/roles]].
- How cents, GST and rounding are handled: [[concepts/money]].
- Words and labels used in the POS: [[concepts/glossary]].
sections.deep:
### Local first, then shared
The register keeps working data on this iPad and shares selected records with Shopify. A completed sale is saved locally before its Shopify upload finishes. Staff, some settings, catalogue and stock are shared or refreshed separately, so two screens can briefly show different update times.
sections.advanced:
### Where to trace a behaviour
Use the topic pages above for the data path, role rules, money calculations and terminology. For an immediate error, start at [[fix]] rather than changing data to make a message disappear.

pages.title: Where data lives and how it syncs
pages.summary: Understand what stays on this iPad, what is shared through Shopify and why a sale can be local before it appears online.
pages.lead: The register stores working data on this iPad and uses Shopify as the shared store for selected records. A sale is saved locally before its upload completes, so a temporary sync delay does not mean the sale disappeared.

sections.basic:
### What lives where
- **On this iPad:** the current cart, local Transactions history, saved carts, cash-drawer ledger, catalogue snapshot, register preferences and queued uploads.
- **In Shopify:** the product catalogue and available stock, customer records, completed Shopify orders, and shared POS data such as sale history, staff and shared settings.
- **On the Zeller terminal:** its pairing and terminal state. Pairing is device-specific and must be set up again if the app is reinstalled or moved to another iPad.

Cash and saved carts can be used offline. Card payments need the network to reach Zeller. A completed sale can stay in the upload queue until the register reconnects.

### What to do when sync is delayed
Check **Notifications** for the exact queued or blocked sale. Reconnect the register and let queued work retry. Correct a Shopify permission or settings error before using **Retry**. Do not make a duplicate sale or clear local history to force an upload. See [[fix/offline-sync]].
sections.deep:
### A sale has a local and shared path
When a sale finishes, the POS writes it to local history and the outbox. The outbox then uploads its steps to Shopify: the order, gift cards where relevant, sale entry and daily roll-up. Each completed step is recorded so a retry can resume. When stock changes elsewhere, registers poll Shopify and update their local snapshots.

An order can therefore be visible in local Transactions while its Shopify order is still pending. The outbox and the CSV history export are separate records; deleting or exporting one does not repair the other.

### Register-specific versus shared settings
The register ID and name, display preferences, cash drawer ledger, screensaver, inventory view and some device state belong to this iPad. Staff, display modes saved on staff, and selected operational settings are shared between registers through Shopify. A settings backup can transfer configuration, but it is not the same as the live sale queue or the catalogue.
sections.advanced:
### Data path
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Finish payment] --> B[Save sale in local POS history]
  B --> C[Add sale to local outbox]
  C --> D[Upload order and shared sale records]
  D -->|success| E[Remove completed outbox item]
  D -->|offline| F[Keep queued for retry]
  G[Shopify catalogue and available stock] --> H[Import or poll to local snapshot]
  I[Register settings and working data] --> J[Persist on this iPad]
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Persist settings, catalogue, cart and local POS data | `hydrate`, `patchSettings`, `patchData`, `patchPos` in `src/state/store.ts` |
| Save a completed sale and queue its upload | `recordSale`, `processOutbox` in `src/lib/sync.ts` |
| Push and pull shared staff/settings and saved carts | `pushSharedSettings`, `pullSettings`, `pushSaved`, `pullSaved` in `src/lib/sync.ts` |
| Import products and poll stock changes | `importFromShopify`, `pollShared` in `src/lib/sync.ts` |
| Export and restore a settings backup | `collectBackup`, `applyBackup` in `src/lib/backupIO.ts` |

The local store is persisted through the app's key-value storage. Shopify is the cross-register shared service; there is no separate POS server for the register's live data.

pages.title: POS glossary
pages.summary: Plain-English meanings for register, Shopify, scanner, staff and payment terms used throughout this help.
pages.lead: Use this page when a POS or Shopify term is unfamiliar. Button names appear in **bold**; code identifiers are shown in `monospace`.

sections.basic:
### Products and stock
- **Variant:** one sellable choice of a Shopify product, such as a particular size or colour.
- **SKU:** the merchant's stock-keeping code for a variant. In Checkout, a scanner can find a variant by its SKU or barcode.
- **Barcode:** the scannable product code stored on a variant. Barcode lookup normalises leading zeroes to match common UPC/EAN formats.
- **Shopify ID / GID:** Shopify's internal identifier for a record. It is not the product code staff should scan at Checkout.
- **Tracked / not tracked:** Shopify either keeps a quantity for this variant or does not. In Inventory, a dash means not tracked; zero is a tracked variant with no available stock.
- **Available:** the Shopify stock quantity the POS imports for the selected location.

### Sales, staff and sync
- **Tender:** how the customer pays: cash, card or gift card.
- **Outbox:** the local queue of completed sales and upload steps waiting to reach Shopify.
- **Cashier pass:** a scannable credential that signs in a staff member; it is different from a product barcode.
- **Role:** Cashier, Manager or Owner access assigned to a staff record.
- **Unknown payment:** the POS cannot yet confirm whether a card payment completed. Check Zeller before charging again.
sections.deep:
### Similar words that mean different things
- A **SKU** is a merchant-defined product code; a Shopify **GID** identifies a record inside Shopify. Scanners should use the variant's barcode or SKU, not its GID.
- A stock count of **0** is not the same as **not tracked**. One is a tracked quantity; the other has no inventory quantity.
- A **queued** sale is saved locally and waiting to upload. A **blocked** sale needs a person to fix the cause before retrying.
- A card **decline** is a known result. An **unknown** result is not a decline and is not safe to retry until checked.

### Guided checkout and price adjustments
- **Guided checkout:** a step-by-step checkout that asks about items, customer, discount, review and payment.
- **Line price:** a chosen price for the whole line and its quantity.
- **Item price:** a chosen unit price for a selected quantity of one item.
- **Whole order price:** a chosen total distributed over eligible cart lines.
- **Adjustment review:** the check before payment that asks staff to keep, change or remove a flagged price adjustment.

pages.title: Money, cents, GST and rounding
pages.summary: See how prices and tenders are represented, when cash rounding applies and how GST appears on receipts.
pages.lead: The POS works in Australian dollars. Prices and payments are kept as whole cents inside the app; cash rounding and GST display follow separate rules.

sections.basic:
### Cents and tender
An amount such as **$12.50** is stored as 1,250 cents. Shopify's decimal prices are converted when they enter or leave the app, which avoids doing normal price arithmetic with floating-point dollar values.

Card payments are charged to the exact remaining amount. If **Cash rounding (5c)** is on, only a cash payment that finishes the sale rounds the amount due to the nearest 5 cents. A cash part-payment is not rounded.

### GST on receipts
In **More ▸ Settings ▸ Receipts**, turn on **Registered for GST** only if the business is registered. The receipt is then titled **Tax invoice** and displays the GST included in GST-inclusive prices; gift-card sale lines are excluded. Check with an accountant before relying on the POS for tax reporting.
sections.deep:
### Cash rounding is not a price change
Rounding changes the final cash due by up to 2 cents. The sale retains its actual price and records the rounding separately. Card tender is never rounded, and a part-payment does not settle the final amount or apply cash rounding.

### GST display
The POS treats displayed item prices as GST-inclusive for this receipt calculation. When GST is enabled, the receipt displays one-eleventh of the eligible GST-inclusive amount as GST. Gift cards are excluded because GST applies when the card is redeemed. This receipt display is not a substitute for Shopify tax configuration, an accounting system or professional tax advice.
sections.advanced:
### Money path
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Shopify decimal price] --> B[Convert to integer cents]
  B --> C[Price cart and discounts in cents]
  C --> D{Tender}
  D -->|Card| E[Charge exact remaining cents]
  D -->|Cash final| F[Optionally round due to 5 cents]
  D -->|Cash part| G[Record exact part payment]
  E --> H[Record actual sale amount]
  F --> H
  G --> H
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Convert dollars and cents, cash rounding | `toCents`, `toDecimal`, `roundCash` in `src/lib/money.ts` |
| Final cash tender and separate rounding record | `cashTender` in `src/lib/saleBuilder.ts` |
| GST-inclusive receipt calculation and gift-card exclusion | `gstIncluded` in `src/lib/receiptDoc.ts` |
| GST registration setting | `ReceiptSettings` in `src/screens/Settings.tsx` |
| Cash rounding preference | `cashRounding` in `src/state/store.ts`, toggle in `src/screens/Settings.tsx` |

GST is a receipt calculation based on the setting and recorded sale lines. It does not change the tender amount or the price stored on the sale.

pages.title: Staff roles and access
pages.summary: Learn what Cashier, Manager and Owner mean, how PIN sign-in affects access and which parts of the More menu are role-gated.
pages.lead: The POS has three roles: **Cashier**, **Manager** and **Owner**. A staff member's role travels with their staff record to the other registers.

sections.basic:
### What each role can open
- **Cashier:** everyday register screens, but not **Reports**, **Staff** or **Settings**.
- **Manager** and **Owner:** can also open Reports, Staff and Settings.

Display modes can hide tabs or More-menu items, but they cannot give a cashier access to manager-only entries. If PINs are not required or no staff members are set up, the register acts as the owner.

### PINs and passes
When **Require PIN to use the register** is on, staff sign in with their PIN or cashier pass. The active staff member is attached to the sale. Switching staff keeps the cart in place. See [[staff]] and [[staff/passes]].
sections.deep:
### Optional price-adjustment restrictions
An owner can choose whether Cashiers or Managers may set item, line or whole-order prices. By default, all roles can set them. A role restriction does not stop staff from removing an adjustment and returning the price to normal. Owners cannot be restricted from setting adjustments.

When an owner exists, only an owner can change these restrictions. If the team has no owner, a manager can manage them so the register does not become impossible to administer. See [[sales/cart-and-prices]] for the adjustment review rules.

### Role and display mode are separate
A staff member's Standard, Simple, Minimal or Custom mode controls presentation, not their role. A cashier cannot use a mode to reveal Reports, Staff or Settings. The only manager or owner keeps Staff and Settings visible even if their chosen mode would otherwise hide those entries, so they can change the mode back. See [[staff/modes]].
sections.advanced:
### Access decision
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Resolve active staff role] --> B{PIN required and staff exists}
  B -->|no| C[Act as owner]
  B -->|yes| D{Signed in staff}
  D -->|manager or owner| E[Show role allowed More entries]
  D -->|cashier or nobody| F[Hide Reports Staff and Settings]
  E --> G[Apply display mode visibility]
  F --> G
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Resolve the active role | `actingRole` in `src/lib/adjustPerms.ts` |
| Gate Reports, Staff and Settings in More | `visibleMoreRows` in `src/lib/uiMode.ts`, `src/screens/More.tsx` |
| Require PIN and create staff records | `src/screens/Staff.tsx` |
| Sign in and switch staff | `src/lib/staffAuth.ts`, `src/screens/StaffLogin.tsx` |
| Configure adjustment restrictions | `canEditAdjustPerms`, `canAdjust` in `src/lib/adjustPerms.ts` |

With PINs enabled, an unknown or locked staff identity resolves to the cashier role. This is the safe default for role-gated screens.

pages.title: When something goes wrong
pages.summary: Start here for card, reader, sync, cash change, stock, keyboard or staff sign-in problems.
pages.lead: Start with the message on screen and choose the closest guide below. If a payment result is uncertain, do not charge again until you have checked whether the first attempt went through.

sections.basic:
### Choose a guide
- Card declined or the customer cannot pay by card: [[fix/card-declined]].
- Reader not ready, not paired or unavailable: [[fix/reader]].
- Sales waiting to upload or a sync error: [[fix/offline-sync]].
- Drawer cannot make the change offered: [[fix/cant-make-change]].
- POS stock differs from Shopify: [[fix/stock-mismatch]].
- HID scanner or keyboard trouble: [[fix/keyboard]].
- Cannot sign in with a PIN or cashier pass: [[fix/locked-out]].

You can also open **More ▸ Help** and search the words shown in the message. Help is bundled in the app and works offline.
sections.deep:
### Avoid repeating uncertain actions
Some actions can have succeeded even when the POS did not receive a clear reply. For an uncertain card result, check the terminal or Zeller dashboard and use the Payment screen's status check or manual resolution before trying another charge. For queued sales, retry the existing upload rather than making a duplicate sale.

### When to ask for help
If the matching guide does not resolve the issue, keep the exact error text and the time it happened. For payment issues, also note whether the terminal showed approved, declined or no result. Do not include card security codes or passwords in a support message.
sections.advanced:
### Support paths
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Read the exact on-screen message] --> B{Which part is affected}
  B -->|Card| C[Check card decline guide]
  B -->|Reader| D[Check reader guide]
  B -->|Sync| E[Check offline sync guide]
  B -->|Cash| F[Check change guide]
  B -->|Stock| G[Check stock mismatch guide]
  B -->|Keyboard| H[Check keyboard guide]
  B -->|Sign in| I[Check locked out guide]
```

| Area | Help page | App location |

| Card result | `fix/card-declined` | Payment screen |
| Reader setup | `fix/reader` | Support & diagnostics |
| Sales sync | `fix/offline-sync` | Notifications |
| Cash change | `fix/cant-make-change` | Cash sheet and drawer |
| Stock | `fix/stock-mismatch` | Inventory |
| Scanner input | `fix/keyboard` | Hardware test and Checkout |
| Staff access | `fix/locked-out` | Sign-in screen and Staff settings |

Each guide names the safest next action for its failure type. Avoid retrying a potentially successful payment or deleting a queued sale as a shortcut.

pages.title: The drawer cannot make change
pages.summary: Respond when the cash drawer ledger cannot make exact change, or check whether a different handover would work.
pages.lead: If the Cash sheet says it **Can't make … change**, the notes and coins recorded in the drawer cannot make that exact amount from the handover and current ledger. Review the displayed options before taking the cash.

sections.basic:
### Choose an offered option
The sheet may offer:
- **Use that smaller handover**: accept a smaller set of the notes the customer gave, return the rest, and make the change from the drawer.
- **Cash … + the rest another way**: take the displayed amount in cash and collect the remaining balance by card or another tender.
- Take the full amount by card.

If the ledger is empty or out of date, count the drawer and correct the ledger first. You can use **The drawer has it (ledger is out of date)** only when you have physically checked that the drawer can provide the displayed change.

### If you have already taken the cash
In **Give change**, the POS suggests notes and coins if it finds an exact combination. Check what you actually hand over, then tap **Gave this**. If needed, choose different denominations manually. You can choose **Done, but don't track it** if you do not want to record the notes and coins.

For the normal cash flow and denominations, see [[pay/cash]] and [[cash/change]].
sections.deep:
### Ledger count versus physical drawer
The suggestion uses the ledger's note and coin counts plus the notes the customer just handed over. If the actual drawer differs from the ledger, the suggestion can be impossible or not match the physical cash. Count or correct the ledger before relying on a suggestion.

The override is a manual acknowledgement that the physical drawer can make the change despite the ledger. The **Give change** step records what was actually handed over when denominations are confirmed; choosing not to track leaves that cash out of the drawer record.

### Do not promise change the drawer cannot make
The POS blocks the normal overpayment path when it cannot make exact change. Ask for a different handover, use the suggested part-cash option, or use another tender. If the customer gives the exact amount, you can take it without tracking denominations.
sections.advanced:
### Change decision
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Tap received notes and coins] --> B{Amount covers cash due}
  B -->|no| C[Ask for more or take part payment]
  B -->|yes exact| D[Take cash]
  B -->|over| E{Drawer plus handover makes exact change}
  E -->|yes| F[Review and confirm notes given]
  E -->|no| G[Offer smaller handover part cash or card]
  G --> H[Override only after physical drawer check]
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Cash sheet prompts and handover options | `src/screens/CashSheet.tsx` |
| Cash amount states, exact-change plan and fallback choices | `cashStatus`, `planChange`, `handBackOptions`, `partCashOption` in `src/lib/cashSale.ts` |
| Note and coin counts | `src/lib/cashLedger.ts`, `src/ui/DenomPad.tsx` |
| Check Change tool | `src/lib/checkChange.ts`, `src/screens/CheckChange.tsx` |

The hardware tender machine is not active. The cashier enters received and given denominations and confirms them manually.

pages.title: Card declined or payment result is unclear
pages.summary: Respond safely to a declined card, interrupted terminal request or payment whose final result is unknown.
pages.lead: Read the result shown on the Payment screen. A clear decline means the card was not accepted; an **unknown** result means the POS has not confirmed whether the customer was charged.

sections.basic:
### A clear decline
Follow the message. Common next steps are to have the customer tap, insert or swipe again, use another card, or split the amount with another payment method. Contact the bank or Zeller if the message says to do so. Do not ask the customer to repeat their PIN where the screen does not request it.

If they want to use another method, select cash, gift card or split payment on the Payment screen. See [[pay/split-and-part]].

### The payment says it is checking or unknown
Do **not** start a second card charge yet. The POS checks the transaction reference with the terminal. If it still cannot confirm the result, check the terminal or Zeller dashboard:
- If it shows approved, choose the option confirming the customer **was** charged.
- If you have checked and it shows the payment did not happen, choose the option confirming the customer **was not** charged.

Only resolve it after checking. Confirming incorrectly can record a payment that was not made or allow a duplicate charge.
sections.deep:
### Declined versus unknown
A clean decline is safe to try again or use another tender.
