A timeout or connection loss after processing began can be ambiguous, so the POS reconciles using the transaction reference and blocks another card charge until resolved. A card-payment failure before the terminal interaction (for example, internet or pairing trouble) is a reader problem; see [[fix/reader]].

The Payment attempt is kept on this device. Reports and sales are not treated as paid until the result is approved or you manually confirm an unknown result.
sections.advanced:
### Payment result path
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Start card payment with unique reference] --> B{Terminal result}
  B -->|Approved| C[Record card tender]
  B -->|Clear decline| D[Use another card or tender]
  B -->|Unknown| E[Reconcile by reference]
  E -->|Found approved| C
  E -->|Still unclear| F[Check terminal or Zeller dashboard]
  F --> G[Manually confirm charged or not charged]
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Decline messages by response code | `lookupResponse` in `src/lib/responseCodes.ts` |
| Normalise terminal responses | `normalise`, `reconcile` in `src/lib/zeller.ts` |
| Payment UI, attempt and manual resolution | `src/screens/Pay.tsx` |
| Read-only attempt list and test purchase | `src/screens/Diagnostics.tsx` |
| Card and split payment guide | `help/pay/card.md`, `help/pay/split-and-part.md` |

`startCharge` records the attempt before calling Zeller. It checks the terminal transaction reference after ambiguous results; never treat a network timeout as a definite decline.

pages.title: Scanner or keyboard input is not working
pages.summary: Check a Bluetooth HID scanner's connection and suffix, then test it in the screen that expects a product or staff code.
pages.lead: A Bluetooth HID scanner behaves like a keyboard: it types the scanned code and usually sends Return. Checkout reads product barcodes or SKUs; staff sign-in reads cashier passes. Check that you are scanning into the right screen. Shopify GIDs are internal IDs, not scanner codes; see [[concepts/glossary]].

sections.basic:
### Test a Bluetooth scanner
1. Check Bluetooth settings on the iPad and make sure the scanner is connected.
2. Open **More ▸ Settings ▸ Hardware** and use **Test scanner**.
3. Scan a known code. A successful test displays the scanned value; it does not add an item to the sale.
4. In **Checkout**, scan a product's barcode or SKU. At staff sign-in, scan the cashier pass instead.

The scanner's suffix must send Return to finish a scan. If the test shows a value without submitting it, set the scanner to append Enter/Return using its manufacturer instructions.

### If characters are missing or out of order
Check that the scanner is connected and test again with the iPad keyboard hidden. Keep the scanner close to the iPad and avoid scanning while another text field is active. Some scanner configurations add a prefix or suffix; reset it to the manufacturer's default barcode/keyboard settings, then configure Return as the suffix.

For supported scanner types and the camera scanner, see [[sales/scanners]].
sections.deep:
### Where the scan goes
Checkout's hidden HID input receives the whole code and submits when Return arrives. It does not grab focus while a real text field or the on-screen keyboard is active. Scanning a product then adds or finds it using the Checkout scan handler. At sign-in, only a cashier-pass code is accepted; an ordinary product code is not a staff login.

The camera scanner is a separate option and does not depend on Bluetooth keyboard focus. You can use it from Checkout or the cashier-pass scanner when those screens offer it.

### If a scan does nothing
- If Test scanner does not show characters, reconnect or pair the scanner with the iPad.
- If Test scanner shows the code but Checkout does not add an item, check that the code is a barcode or SKU on an imported variant, and that the correct register/location is loaded.
- If the scanner types into a name or search field, finish or close that field before scanning again.
- If staff sign-in says the code is not a pass, use the cashier's issued pass or enter their PIN.
sections.advanced:
### HID input path
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Scanner types code] --> B[Hidden HID input collects characters]
  B --> C{Return suffix received}
  C -->|yes| D[Submit complete code]
  C -->|no| E[Check scanner suffix configuration]
  D --> F{Current screen}
  F -->|Checkout| G[Look up product barcode or SKU]
  F -->|Staff sign in| H[Validate cashier pass]
  B --> I[Do not steal focus from a real field]
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| HID and camera scanning | `HidScanner`, `CameraScanner` in `src/screens/Scanner.tsx` |
| Checkout barcode/SKU handling | `onScan` in `src/screens/Checkout.tsx`, `findByBarcode` in `src/lib/cartOps.ts` |
| Pass scanning at sign-in | `StaffLoginPad` in `src/screens/StaffLogin.tsx` |
| Scanner test and connection instructions | `src/screens/Settings.tsx`, `help/settings/hardware.md` |
| Avoid taking focus from an active text field | `isUserTyping` in `src/lib/focusGuard.ts` |

The hidden field is keyed again after each Return to clear the previous scan before the next one.

pages.title: Cannot sign in or a cashier pass will not scan
pages.summary: Recover from an incorrect PIN or cashier pass, and identify who can change staff access.
pages.lead: Check whether the register expects a staff PIN or an issued cashier pass. A forgotten PIN cannot be recovered from the POS; ask an owner or manager who can still sign in to manage the staff record.

sections.basic:
### Check the sign-in method
- Enter the PIN assigned to your staff account. PINs are 4–6 digits.
- For a pass, scan the current cashier pass barcode. A cancelled or replaced pass no longer signs in.
- If the pass is not recognised, use the PIN or ask an owner to check your Staff record and issue a replacement.

An owner can open **More ▸ Staff**, select your name, and issue or replace your cashier pass. The app does not show an existing PIN. If your PIN is forgotten, ask an owner to remove the old staff record and add you again with a new PIN and the correct role. Have the owner verify that another owner remains before removing any owner account.

### If nobody can sign in
Do not delete the app or clear its data; that can remove local sales and settings. Use a working owner account on another register to check shared staff settings, then contact your POS administrator or support if no owner account remains available.
sections.deep:
### Pass versus PIN
A cashier pass is a scannable credential tied to one staff record. Replacing or cancelling the pass invalidates the previous code. A pass can be printed or added to Apple Wallet; it is not a backup of the staff account or a way to reveal the PIN.

PINs are stored as salted hashes and shared with the other registers through Shopify settings. They cannot be read back as plain digits. A replacement PIN is set by adding a new staff record after removing the old one.

### Keep an owner available
Before removing a staff member, confirm that the team will still have an owner able to manage staff and settings. A register with no available owner may require administrator/support assistance to restore access.
sections.advanced:
### Sign-in path
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Open sign in] --> B{Credential}
  B -->|PIN| C[Verify staff PIN]
  B -->|Pass| D[Validate cashier pass]
  C --> E{Valid}
  D --> E
  E -->|yes| F[Set active staff]
  E -->|no| G[Show sign in error]
  G --> H[Ask an owner to restore access]
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Verify PIN and cashier pass | `signInWithPin`, `signInWithPass` in `src/lib/staffAuth.ts` |
| Store salted PIN hashes | `hashPin`, `verifyPin` in `src/lib/pin.ts` |
| Add or remove staff and issue a pass | `src/screens/Staff.tsx`, `src/screens/StaffPass.tsx` |
| Scan a pass at sign-in | `src/screens/StaffLogin.tsx` |

Staff PINs are not recoverable from a backup as plain text. To protect local data, do not reinstall the app as a PIN-reset step.

pages.title: Offline, queued sales and sync errors
pages.summary: Check connectivity, understand queued sale uploads and retry a blocked upload without duplicating the sale.
pages.lead: Sales are saved on this iPad first, then uploaded to Shopify when the connection is available. If a sale is queued, leave it in place; do not ring it through again just to make it appear online.

sections.basic:
### Check the sync status
Open **Notifications**. A queued sale says it will upload when the connection is back. A blocked sale shows an error and a **Retry** button.
- If the iPad is offline, reconnect it to Wi-Fi or another working network and leave the POS open.
- If Shopify credentials or permissions were rejected, fix the Shopify connection in **More ▸ Settings ▸ Shopify** before retrying.
- After fixing the cause, tap **Retry** on the blocked sale. The POS resumes its saved upload steps.

Cash and saved carts can work offline. Card payments require an internet connection to reach Zeller. To set up Shopify again, see [[settings/shopify]].

### If the sale stays queued
Check the exact error on Notifications and make sure the iPad can reach Shopify. The app retries automatically when it processes the outbox; keep the app open and connected. A blocked sale needs the cause corrected and an explicit **Retry**.
sections.deep:
### The sale is not lost or duplicated
The POS records the completed sale locally and adds it to an upload queue. Upload steps use stable identifiers so a retry can resume rather than create a second order. A network failure leaves the sale queued; a Shopify user/permission error blocks that item until corrected.

The device's local Transactions history can show the sale while Shopify is still catching up. The catalogue and stock updates may also take time to refresh on other registers.

### What not to do
- Do not make a second POS sale for the same customer purchase just because the upload has not finished.
- Do not clear local history to fix a queue. CSV history and the sale upload queue are separate.
- Do not repeatedly retry a blocked permission/configuration error without correcting its cause first.
sections.advanced:
### Outbox retry path
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Complete sale and save locally] --> B[Add sale to outbox]
  B --> C[Upload idempotent steps to Shopify]
  C -->|success| D[Remove completed outbox item]
  C -->|network error| E[Keep queued and retry later]
  C -->|Shopify user error| F[Mark blocked and show Retry]
  F --> G[Fix credentials or Shopify setting]
  G --> H[Retry existing outbox item]
  H --> C
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Process and retry sale uploads | `processOutbox`, `retryBlocked` in `src/lib/sync.ts` |
| Locally stored sales and outbox | `Pos`, `OutboxItem` in `src/state/store.ts` |
| Queue status and Retry button | `src/screens/Notifications.tsx` |
| Network vs Shopify configuration errors | `isNetworkError`, `ShopifyUserError` in `src/lib/shopify/client.ts` |
| Shopify credentials and import | `src/screens/Settings.tsx`, `help/settings/shopify.md` |

Completed outbox steps are marked individually. A retry skips those steps and uses the stored sale data for the work that remains.

pages.title: Reader not ready or pairing
pages.summary: Check the Zeller terminal connection, pair it again if needed, and distinguish reader trouble from a card decline.
pages.lead: If the Payment screen says the reader is not ready, open **More ▸ Support & diagnostics** and check the Zeller reader status before starting another card payment.

sections.basic:
### Check or pair the reader
1. Make sure the terminal is on and connected to the network.
2. Open **More ▸ Support & diagnostics**.
3. Tap **Check reader**. If it is not paired, tap **Setup (pair terminal)** and follow the terminal's prompts.
4. When the status says ready, return to the sale and try again.

If the terminal is serving another register, wait for that payment to finish before retrying. Card payments need an internet connection; cash can still be taken offline.

### Test after setup
In Support & diagnostics, **Test purchase $1.00** makes a real $1.00 card transaction. Use it only when you intend to test with a card. If approved, the screen offers **Refund the $1.00 test**.
sections.deep:
### Reader trouble or card decline?
- **Reader not ready**, **not paired**, **offline** or **terminal unavailable** means the POS cannot start or reach the terminal. Check power, network and pairing.
- **Card declined** means the terminal returned a card or issuer decision. Follow [[fix/card-declined]] instead of repeatedly pairing the reader.
- If the customer may already have been charged, treat the outcome as unknown and check the terminal or Zeller dashboard before another attempt.

The POS keeps the Zeller provider mounted for the entire app session. If the app was reinstalled, pair the terminal again. Reader pairing is device-specific and is not carried in a backup.
sections.advanced:
### Reader diagnostic path
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Open Support and diagnostics] --> B[Check reader]
  B --> C{Ready}
  C -->|no| D[Check power and network]
  D --> E[Setup pair terminal]
  E --> B
  C -->|yes| F[Return to the Payment screen]
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Reader status, pairing and test purchase | `src/screens/Diagnostics.tsx` |
| One terminal handle and pairing calls | `checkReader`, `pairReader` in `App.tsx` |
| Reader issue notifications | `src/zellerBridge.tsx`, `src/screens/Pay.tsx` |
| Terminal response mapping | `src/lib/zeller.ts` |
| Payment settings and Reader & pairing entry | `src/screens/Settings.tsx` |

Setup and check run through the Zeller SDK. If setup returns an error, read the message in the diagnostic screen; the app does not mark the reader ready until initialisation succeeds.

pages.title: Stock counts differ from Shopify
pages.summary: Refresh the selected location's stock, check variant tracking and distinguish local sales from Shopify's available quantity.
pages.lead: Inventory shows stock for the Shopify location selected on this register. Refresh from Shopify before comparing, and make sure you are looking at the same location and variant in both places.

sections.basic:
### Refresh the catalogue and stock
1. Check the location in **More ▸ Settings ▸ Shopify**.
2. Open **Inventory** and tap **Refresh stock from Shopify**.
3. In **Filters & sort**, check the import time and total variants on this iPad.
4. Search by variant name, SKU or barcode and check that the product status and stock filters do not hide it.

If this register is connected to the wrong location, select the correct active location and refresh again. For the filter meanings and stock update controls, see [[stock/inventory]].

### Check whether the item is tracked
**—** means inventory is not tracked; **0** means tracked and currently out of stock. A negative number means more units have been sold than the available count. Check the tracked setting and available quantity for that exact variant in Shopify.
sections.deep:
### Why registers can temporarily differ
Shopify is the shared source. Each register keeps a local catalogue and stock snapshot. Sales update this register's local count immediately, while the sale upload and the other registers' stock refresh happen separately. A register that is offline or has not polled yet can show an older count.

The POS reads the selected location's **available** quantity. Shopify's other inventory states or another location may not match that number.

### When a sale is queued
A completed sale reduces the local count and queues its Shopify order. If it is still queued, correct the sync issue rather than adjusting stock to make the local display look right. See [[fix/offline-sync]].
sections.advanced:
### Stock update and refresh path
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Choose active Shopify location] --> B[Import variants and available quantity]
  B --> C[Save local catalogue snapshot]
  D[Complete a sale] --> E[Reduce local stock]
  E --> F[Upload order to Shopify]
  F --> G[Other registers refresh stock delta]
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Select location and full catalogue import | `src/screens/Settings.tsx`, `importFromShopify` in `src/lib/sync.ts` |
| Read tracked and available stock | `fetchVariants` in `src/lib/shopify/catalogue.ts` |
| Poll location stock changes | `fetchStockDelta` in `src/lib/shopify/catalogue.ts`, `pollShared` in `src/lib/sync.ts` |
| Mirror completed sale stock locally | `applyLocalStock` in `src/lib/sync.ts` |
| Set or adjust stock from the POS | `src/screens/Inventory.tsx`, `src/lib/shopify/inventory.ts` |

Compare the same variant, location and Shopify quantity name (**available**). A manual Inventory count or adjustment writes to Shopify; do not use one to conceal a delayed sync.

pages.title: Selling gift cards
pages.summary: Add a gift card to a sale, choose handover or email, and find its code and QR after payment.
pages.lead: Sell a gift card from **More ▸ Gift cards** or the **Sell gift card** tile. The card is created in Shopify only after the sale is paid.

sections.basic:
### Add a gift card to a sale
1. Tap **Sell gift card** and choose a suggested amount, or enter an amount with the keypad and tap **Next**.
2. Choose how the customer will get it: **Hand over / print** or **Email it**.
3. For email delivery, enter the recipient's email. Name and message are optional. You can copy the current cart customer's email with the offered chip.
4. Tap **Add gift card to cart**. It is now a line in the cart, not a live gift card yet. Finish taking payment as usual.

Shopify creates the card after payment completes and sends the recipient email when an address was entered. A failed creation stays queued for retry; do not sell a second card just because creation is delayed.

### Give the customer the code
After payment, the receipt screen shows the gift card code and a **Gift card QR (for scanning at a register)**. Show or print that QR for the customer. It contains the gift card code for scanning at checkout.

If you chose **Hand over / print** and left the recipient email blank, the receipt may also offer **Claim QR: customer adds their email** when the claim page is configured. The customer scans it and enters their email later: [[gift/claim-page]].

### Check cards later
Use **More ▸ Gift cards** to **Check balance** or view a card's history. See [[gift/check-redeem]]. To take a gift card as payment, open Payment and tap **Gift card**: [[pay/gift-card]].
sections.deep:
### The card is made after payment
Adding the gift card to the cart reserves its amount and generates a code for the sale, but it does not create a Shopify gift card yet. Once payment is complete, the sale sync creates the Shopify card. This avoids creating cards for abandoned or declined sales. If sync is offline or Shopify fails, the paid sale remains queued and the create step can retry safely.

When **Email it** is selected, the recipient email, optional name and optional message are attached to the gift card. Shopify sends the card email after creation. The app does not send a second email.

### Receipts and QR codes
The **Gift card QR** is for scanning the card code at a register. The **Claim QR** is different: it opens the shop's claim page so a recipient can add their email when no email was entered at sale time. It is only offered when the claim page URL and secret are set in Settings ▸ Gift cards.

The code is visible on the receipt screen after sale. Treat it like cash: anyone with an active card's code may be able to spend its balance.

### If the card does not appear
Check that the sale completed and the register is online. A card can be waiting for sync; check again after the outbox syncs. If Shopify creation keeps failing, open the sync issue and ask an owner to investigate rather than making another gift card line.
sections.advanced:
### Sale-to-card flow
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Choose value and delivery] --> B[Add gift card line with a code]
  B --> C{Sale payment completed}
  C -->|no| D[No Shopify card is created]
  C -->|yes| E[Sale enters the sync outbox]
  E --> F[Create Shopify gift card]
  F -->|recipient email| G[Shopify sends the card email]
  F -->|no email| H[Receipt shows code and QR]
  H --> I[Optional claim QR if configured]
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Sell flow and recipient fields | `GiftSellSheet` in `src/screens/sheets.tsx` |
| Gift card hub | `src/screens/GiftCards.tsx` |
| Cart line and delivery data | `addGiftCardLine` in `src/lib/cartOps.ts`; `GiftRecipient` in `src/lib/types.ts` |
| Create after payment and retry safely | outbox processing in `src/lib/sync.ts` |
| Shopify create and email | `createGiftCard` in `src/lib/shopify/giftcards.ts` |
| Receipt code and QR | `src/screens/Receipt.tsx`, `giftQrPayload` in `src/lib/giftCode.ts` |
| Claim QR | `claimUrl` in `src/lib/giftClaim.ts` |

The sync outbox records completed gift-card codes in `giftDone`, so a retry skips cards already created. Card creation is idempotent by code. A sale with no email can still show a claim QR if the claim service is configured.

### Known receipt detail
The immediate receipt document currently prints the full gift card code in its payment line; the Shopify order keeps only the last four characters. Handle the immediate receipt link and its QR as sensitive. See the open note N30 in `docs/PROGRESS.md`.

pages.title: Checking and redeeming gift cards
pages.summary: Check a balance and history without paying, understand the card QR, and use a gift card at checkout.
pages.lead: Check a gift card before a sale without changing its balance, or apply it as a payment during checkout.

sections.basic:
### Check a balance
Open **More ▸ Gift cards** and tap **Check balance**, or use **Check gift card** from the cart menu. Type the code or tap **Scan** and scan the gift card QR. Tap **Check**. The sheet shows its balance, last four characters, and whether it is **Active** or **Disabled**. If the card can be found, the Gift cards screen can also show its recent credits and redemptions.

Checking a balance does not use any of it. To pay with the card, use the **Gift card** button on the Payment screen: [[pay/gift-card]].

### Scan the right QR
- **Gift card QR (for scanning at a register):** contains the card code. Use it to check a balance or pay with the card.
- **Claim QR: customer adds their email:** opens the claim page so the recipient can give Shopify their email. It does not contain the spendable card code. See [[gift/claim-page]].
- A QR with a `shopify-giftcard` prefix is cleaned automatically. You do not need to edit it.

### Messages
- **No gift card found for that code.** Check the printed code or scan the Gift card QR again.
- **Lookup failed** with a reason: the POS could not reach Shopify. Check the connection and try again.
- **Disabled:** the card cannot be used. Ask an owner to check it in Shopify.
- **code could not be verified:** the card may have been created outside this POS. The POS can only accept it when it finds one unmarked candidate and the entered code is long enough.
sections.deep:
### What a balance check reads
Shopify holds the card's current balance and enabled status. The POS searches candidate cards by their last four characters, then checks the full code against a fingerprint stored on cards created by the POS. For a card made elsewhere, it can show an unverified result when exactly one candidate is unmarked and the code has at least eight characters. Otherwise it reports no card found.

The Gift cards screen shows the 30 most recent card transactions when available. Credits add value; redemptions take value off. The Sales report gives totals for gift cards sold, redeemed and outstanding; it is not the history of one individual card.

### Paying with a card
At payment, **Use as payment** takes the lesser of the current payment amount and the card's balance. Shopify is charged immediately. If that does not cover the whole sale, the unpaid amount remains for another tender. A balance check alone does not reserve or debit the card.

If a part-paid sale is cancelled after the card was charged, the POS cannot automatically put that amount back. Ask someone authorised to correct the card in Shopify. See [[pay/gift-card]] for the full payment steps.
sections.advanced:
### Balance check and payment
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Type code or scan card QR] --> B[Strip QR prefix and normalise code]
  B --> C[Find Shopify card by last four and checksum]
  C -->|not found| D[Show no card found]
  C -->|found| E[Show balance and status]
  E --> F{Check only}
  F -->|yes| G[No balance change]
  F -->|payment| H{Active with balance}
  H -->|no| I[Cannot use as payment]
  H -->|yes| J[Debit the smaller of balance and amount due]
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Gift cards hub and history | `src/screens/GiftCards.tsx` |
| Check code and balance sheet | `GiftCheckSheet` in `src/screens/sheets.tsx` |
| Code normalisation and QR prefix | `stripGiftPrefix`, `normaliseCode` in `src/lib/giftCode.ts` |
| Lookup and transaction history | `lookupGiftCard`, `giftCardHistory` in `src/lib/shopify/giftcards.ts` |
| Payment debit | `useGift` in `src/screens/Pay.tsx`; `debitGiftCard` in `src/lib/shopify/giftcards.ts` |
| Gift-card report totals | `outstandingBalance` in `src/lib/shopify/giftcards.ts`; `src/screens/Reports.tsx` |

`lookupGiftCard` returns the balance and status but makes no debit. `useGift` calls Shopify's debit mutation before adding the tender to the payment list. Gift cards are not cash, are not rounded, and do not change the cash drawer ledger.

pages.title: The gift card claim page
pages.summary: Configure the optional claim Worker so someone can add a name and email to a gift card sold without a recipient.
pages.lead: The claim page is an optional website for gift cards sold without an email address. The customer scans a QR on the receipt, enters their name and email, and Shopify sends the gift card to them.

sections.basic:
### Set it up
1. Deploy the separate Worker in `gift-claim-server/` using its README. It needs its own Shopify app and a `CLAIMS` KV namespace.
2. In the app, open **Settings ▸ Gift cards ▸ Gift card claim page**.
3. Enter the deployed Worker URL and the same secret used as its `CLAIM_SECRET`.
4. Save the settings. Leave the URL blank to turn off claim QR codes.

The regular email-at-sale flow does not need this Worker. For that, choose **Email it** when adding a gift card: [[gift]].

### What the customer does
After a gift card sale without an email address, open the receipt and tap **Claim QR: customer adds their email**. The customer scans it with a phone camera, enters their name and email, and submits. The page confirms when the email has been sent. Each card can be claimed once.

The QR is a claim link, not the card's spending code. The separate **Gift card QR** is for scanning the card at a register: [[gift/check-redeem]].

### If the QR is missing or fails
- **No Claim QR button:** check that the claim page URL and secret are set, and that the gift card line has no recipient email.
- **This link is not valid:** check the configured secret matches the Worker secret, and use the QR from the receipt without editing its link.
- **Already claimed:** the card already has a recipient or its claim was completed. Contact the shop if the email went to the wrong person.
- **Something went wrong:** ask the customer to retry in a minute. If it keeps failing, check the Worker and Shopify connection.
sections.deep:
### What the claim page changes
The Worker checks that the signed link belongs to a gift card created by this POS, finds an enabled card, and confirms it has not already been sent to a recipient. It then asks for the recipient's name, email and optional message, saves recipient details on the card, and asks Shopify to send its notification. It does not change the card's balance.

The page reveals only the card's last four characters. The claim link itself is sensitive: anyone who has the receipt QR can claim the card, so give it to the intended recipient.

### One claim and retry behaviour
The Worker stores a claim marker before it updates the card and sends the email, to prevent a double tap from sending twice. If the operation fails, it removes the marker so the customer can retry. The Worker also has an approximate per-IP request limit.

### Keep the secrets aligned
The POS signs the claim link with the secret saved in Settings. The Worker checks it with `CLAIM_SECRET`. If the values differ, the link cannot be verified. The Worker uses a separate Shopify app from the POS and needs permission to read and update gift cards and customers.
sections.advanced:
### Claim request flow
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[POS signs card code into claim QR] --> B[Customer opens signed link]
  B --> C{Link valid and card enabled}
  C -->|no| D[Show help message]
  C -->|yes| E{Already has recipient or claimed}
  E -->|yes| F[Show already claimed]
  E -->|no| G[Customer submits name and email]
  G --> H[Save recipient and send Shopify email]
  H --> I[Show confirmation]
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Settings URL and secret | `Gift card claim page` in `src/screens/Settings.tsx` |
| Signed claim URL | `claimUrl` in `src/lib/giftClaim.ts` |
| Receipt QR and eligibility | `ReceiptPrompt` in `src/screens/Receipt.tsx` |
| Token verification and form validation | `verifyClaimToken`, `validateClaim` in `gift-claim-server/src/claim.ts` |
| Find card, save recipient and send | Worker handler in `gift-claim-server/src/index.ts` |
| Worker setup | `gift-claim-server/README.md` |

The token contains a normalised gift card code and a truncated HMAC-SHA-256 signature. The Worker finds only cards whose note checksum matches, and stores claim state in the `CLAIMS` KV namespace. KV is not atomic, so simultaneous requests have a small race window; Shopify remains the card balance and recipient record.

### Limits
The claim page is not Shopify's own gift-card storefront page. It collects the recipient details and triggers Shopify's gift card email. It works only for cards created by this POS with a matching checksum, and requires a live Worker, KV and Shopify connection.

pages.title: Orders and transactions
pages.summary: Find past sales, distinguish Shopify orders from the transaction timeline, and open a sale, refund, or receipt.
pages.lead: Use **More ▸ Orders** to manage Shopify orders. Use the **Transactions** tab to search the register's sales, refunds and imported Square history.

sections.basic:
### Orders
In **More ▸ Orders**, use **Open**, **Unfulfilled** and **Completed** to filter Shopify POS orders. Pull down to refresh. Tap an order to see its lines and choose **Mark fulfilled**, **Refund or return**, or **Receipt**. **Mark fulfilled** is hidden when Shopify already shows the order as fulfilled.

### Transactions
Open the **Transactions** tab. Completed local sales and refunds appear newest first, grouped by day. Tap one to see the lines and tenders. If an entry says **Waiting to sync to Shopify**, the sale is still local and a return is unavailable until its Shopify order exists.

Type a receipt number, customer, note or item to filter the loaded transactions. Press Search to look in Shopify for matching POS orders. **Load more** fetches the next page of orders. Tap **Square history** to include imported Square sales; those entries are read-only and cannot be returned here.

### Receipts and returns
Open a transaction and tap **New receipt** to show receipt options again. A Shopify-backed sale can offer **Return or exchange**: [[orders/refunds]]. Square history is read-only. Receipt delivery options are in [[pay/receipts]]. Sales totals and comparisons are in [[orders/reports]], and imported Square records are covered in [[orders/square-history]].
sections.deep:
### Orders and Transactions are different views
Orders is a live Shopify view with fulfillment filters and actions. Transactions combines local sale records with Shopify orders, so a sale can appear there before its order has finished syncing. Once Shopify returns the order, the transaction row can link to it and the return action becomes available.

The Square history chip adds previously imported Square records to Transactions; it does not write them to Shopify. It loads them from the history files on this iPad. Do not treat the Square entries as live Shopify orders.

### Search and loading
Transactions first filters entries already loaded on the device and the current order page. Press **Search Shopify** to ask Shopify for matching POS-tagged orders. The standard list loads recent Shopify orders in pages of 25; **Load more** requests the next cursor. Orders loads up to 30 for its selected status each time it refreshes.

If an order or transaction is missing, check the date, the active view, and whether the sale has synced. Square records appear only while Square history is selected and available on this device.
sections.advanced:
### Transaction sources
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Local sales and refunds] --> C[Transactions timeline]
  B[Shopify POS-tagged orders] --> C
  D[Square history when selected] --> C
  C --> E[Open detail and receipt]
  E --> F{Shopify order available}
  F -->|yes| G[Return or exchange may be available]
  F -->|no| H[Wait for sync]
  D --> I[Read only]
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Orders filters and actions | `src/screens/Orders.tsx` |
| Transactions timeline and search | `src/screens/Transactions.tsx` |
| Shopify order list and fulfillment | `listOrders`, `fulfillOrder` in `src/lib/shopify/orders.ts` |
| Shopify POS order tag and mapped order | `src/lib/shopify/orderModel.ts` |
| Local completed sales | `src/state/store.ts` |
| Imported Square transactions | `loadSquareSales` in `src/lib/squareHistoryIO.ts` |
| Refund flow | `src/screens/Refund.tsx` |

Shopify list queries use the `tag:pos` filter. The local list merges records by sale UUID to avoid showing the local sale and its Shopify order twice. Transactions search matches the loaded entries locally, then optionally sends a POS-tagged query to Shopify.

pages.title: Refunds and exchanges
pages.summary: Choose what is coming back, select a refund method, restock items, and charge or refund the difference on an exchange.
pages.lead: Start a return from a Shopify order or a synced sale in Transactions. Choose the items or amount, decide whether to restock, then confirm the refund or exchange.

sections.basic:
### Start a return
1. Open **More ▸ Orders** or **Transactions**, open the Shopify-backed sale, and tap **Refund or return** or **Return or exchange**.
2. In **Items**, use **+** and **−** to choose quantities, up to the refundable amount. Or switch to **Amount** and enter a value.
3. Add replacement items if this is an exchange. Their current prices and discounts are included.
4. Choose a **Reason** and whether to **Restock returned items**.
5. Choose where money goes: **Original**, **Cash** or **Gift card**, then tap the button showing the refund, charge or even exchange.
6. Confirm. If the customer owes more for replacement items, the remaining amount goes to Payment. If cash is owed, the sheet tells you what to hand over.

For **Original**, the screen shows the amounts still refundable by card, cash and gift card. A card refund needs the Zeller terminal.

### What happens next
- **Refund:** return value is greater than replacement value. The difference goes to the selected refund method.
- **Charge:** replacement items cost more. The customer pays the difference at Payment.
- **Even exchange:** the values match; there is no amount to collect or return.
- **Restock returned items** adds the returned quantity back to Shopify stock when the refund is recorded.
- A new gift card refund shows its code when complete. Give the customer that code.

### If something goes wrong
- **Reader not ready:** a card refund needs the Zeller terminal. Pair or reconnect it, then try again.
- **Card refund status is unknown:** check the Zeller dashboard before retrying; do not issue the same refund twice.
- **Refund taken but Shopify did not record it:** the money has already been returned. Check Notifications and ask an owner to reconcile Shopify before retrying.
- If Shopify says only part can go back to the original methods, the refund is larger than the unrefunded amounts those methods received.
sections.deep:
### Refund limits and methods
The app reads successful sale and refund transactions from Shopify to calculate what remains refundable for each original tender. **Original** routes card value back through Zeller, gift card value to the original card when its id is available, and cash as cash. Choosing **Cash** or **Gift card** directs the refund to that method instead. Zeller card refunds are processed before the Shopify refund record is written.

The amount mode cannot exceed the remaining refundable total. The selected returned lines determine which Shopify order lines are included. The reason is saved with the POS refund; Shopify receives the reason with `(POS)` appended.

### Exchanges
Replacement products are added to a temporary cart and priced using the current catalogue and discounts. The value of returned goods is compared with the replacement total. If the replacement total is higher, the difference is paid as a normal sale using exchange credit first. If it is lower, the difference is refunded using the selected method.

### Cash and gift card refunds
For a cash refund, the cashier physically hands over the money. The **Give cash refund** sheet can suggest notes and coins from the drawer or let the cashier enter the notes actually given. Confirming the denomination list updates the local ledger; **Done, but don't track it** does not. Gift-card refunds credit the original card when possible, or create a new gift card; the new code is shown when complete.
sections.advanced:
### Refund sequence
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Choose return lines or amount] --> B[Choose replacement items and reason]
  B --> C[Choose refund method and restock]
  C --> D{Card amount}
  D -->|yes| E[Refund through Zeller terminal]
  D -->|no| F[Credit gift card or prepare cash]
  E --> G[Record refund in Shopify]
  F --> G
  G --> H[Write local refund record]
  H --> I{Replacement items}
  I -->|yes| J[Open Payment for difference]
  I -->|no| K[Show completion or cash handover]
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Return screen and choices | `RefundScreen` in `src/screens/Refund.tsx` |
| Refund tender plan | `planRefund`, `refundableByGateway` in `src/lib/returns.ts` |
| Execute tender refunds and local record | `executeRefund` in `src/lib/refundFlow.ts` |
| Shopify refund and stock restock | `refundOrderInShopify` in `src/lib/shopify/orders.ts` |
| Card refund | `startRefund` in `src/lib/zeller.ts` |
| Cash handover | `GiveCashSheet` in `src/screens/CashSheet.tsx`; `postCashRefund` in `src/lib/cashSale.ts` |

### Important failure boundary
Card refunds happen before Shopify's `refundCreate`. If Shopify recording fails after money was returned, the app logs an error and adds a Notifications entry; it does not silently reverse the tender. For an unknown Zeller result, verify the transaction in Zeller before starting another refund.

pages.title: Reports
pages.summary: Choose a reporting period and register, compare sales, read payment and category totals, and understand gift card totals.
pages.lead: **Reports** summarises sales records from this and other registers, plus imported Square history when it is available.

sections.basic:
### Choose what to view
Open **More ▸ Reports**. The Sales tab starts on **1W**. Choose **1D**, **1W**, **1M**, **3M**, **1Y**, or **Custom**. Custom lets you enter start and end dates as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

Choose **Prev period** or **Last year** to compare, or **No compare** to hide the comparison. Tap **Customise** to choose **All devices** or one register. Imported Square data is labelled **Square (old)**.

### Read the Sales report
The report shows Gross sales, Discounts, Refunds, Net sales, Total collected, estimated Card fees, Net after fees, COGS, Gross profit, payment types and top categories. Price adjustments, when present, are listed by reason; their savings are already included in Discounts.

Tap **Refresh** to fetch shared reports again. Tap the share button in the top bar to export the current sales range and category totals as text.

### Gift card report
Switch to **Gift cards** for value of cards sold in the selected period, gift-card payments redeemed in that period, and the total balance across all active cards. Tap **Gift cards** to open the card hub and check an individual card.

For cash notes and drawer banking, use [[cash/float-report]] instead. Older imported Square sales are explained in [[orders/square-history]].
sections.deep:
### What the totals mean
- **Gross sales**, discounts and refunds make up **Net sales**. Gift card sales are shown separately in the rollup, not as ordinary item sales.
- **Total collected** includes net sales and gift card sales, minus other refunds.
- **Card fees (est. 1.4%)** are an estimate and are not taken off Net sales. **Net after fees** subtracts that estimate.
- **COGS** is shown separately; **Gross profit** is Net sales minus COGS.
- **Payment types** shows the amounts recorded for each tender. **Top categories** shows the leading categories by gross sales.

The comparison uses the same selected date range shifted to the previous period or the corresponding period last year. Selecting a register filters both the current totals and comparison.

### Where register data comes from
Shopify shared rollups are loaded when connected. Local register rollups and sales that are still waiting in the outbox are included. Imported Square rollups are added under their own **Square (old)** register. When data has not synced, registers are offline, or historical records are missing, totals may not match Shopify analytics yet.

The outstanding gift card figure is the balance of all active cards read from Shopify; it is not restricted to the selected sales period or register. The sold and redeemed figures are period-based.
sections.advanced:
### Report data flow
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Local and outbox sales] --> D[Build report totals for chosen dates]
  B[Shopify shared rollups] --> D
  C[Square history rollups] --> D
  D --> E[Filter by register and compare]
  E --> F[Show totals and categories]
  G[Gift cards tab] --> H[Period gift sales and redemptions]
  G --> I[Read all active balances from Shopify]
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Report screen and filters | `src/screens/Reports.tsx` |
| Combine local, remote, outbox and Square data | `useRollups` in `src/screens/Reports.tsx` |
| Period aggregation and derived totals | `src/lib/rollup.ts` |
| Gift card outstanding total | `outstandingBalance` in `src/lib/shopify/giftcards.ts` |
| Imported Square rollups | `loadSquareRollups` in `src/lib/squareHistoryIO.ts` |

The report labels this **Card fees (est. 1.4%)**. It does not read Zeller fee statements; POS sale records use the card fee rate configured for the register when the sale was made (1.4% card-present by default). Square's imported history can include its actual card fees. See [[orders/square-history]].

### If a number looks unexpected
- Check the date range and register selector first.
- Press **Refresh** when online. Local or outbox sales can be ahead of shared Shopify rollups.
- Check whether Square history is included as a separate register.
- Treat estimated card fees as an estimate, not a settlement figure.

pages.title: Square history
pages.summary: Export old Square sales on a PC, import them onto each register, and understand how they appear in Reports and Transactions.
pages.lead: Square history is a one-time, read-only import of old Square sales and refunds. It never changes Shopify items, stock or customers.

sections.basic:
### Export from Square
On a PC, follow `tools/square-history/README.md`: create a Square developer app, put its production access token in the local `.env`, then run the export script. Choose a date range with `--from` and `--to`, or omit them to export the available history. Keep the script running while the iPad imports.

### Import to each iPad
On the iPad, open **Settings ▸ Square history** and either:
1. Tap **Scan QR from PC** while the PC and iPad are on the same Wi-Fi.
2. Type the address printed by the script and tap **Import from address**.
3. Copy the files from the PC's `out` folder to the iPad and tap **Pick files**.

The import shows how many sales and refunds were loaded and how many item lines matched a Shopify variant. After import, the PC script can be stopped. Repeat the import on each register that needs this history.

### Find the imported records
Imported sales appear in Reports as **Square (old)** and in Transactions when the **Square history** chip is selected. They are historical and read-only: they cannot be refunded from this POS.

If you refresh the Shopify catalogue, tap **Re-match to Shopify catalogue** in Settings ▸ Square history. Use **Delete imported Square history** to remove it from this iPad.
sections.deep:
### What is imported and matched
Completed sales and refunds are included. Square variations link to Shopify variants by SKU first, then UPC/barcode. A match gets Shopify's item name, cost and category for reports. An unmatched line stays a custom Square line, with Square's category. The import also carries over Square's tender details, discounts, tips, fees and customer names on their sales; it does not create Shopify customer records.

### Where the files live
History is stored compressed in monthly files under the app's `Documents/square-history/` folder. Reports use a small daily rollup file; Transactions reads the detailed monthly files. Re-match rebuilds the links and report rollups from those local files without contacting Square.

### Connection and import problems
- **Timed out / could not reach the PC:** use the same Wi-Fi, leave the export script running, check the local-network permission in iOS Settings, or transfer the output files and use **Pick files**.
- **No matching SKU:** refresh Shopify catalogue, then re-match. A missing match does not lose the sale; it remains a custom line.
- **Wrong or incomplete date range:** rerun the PC export with the desired dates and import the resulting files.
- The PC script serves only the export folder while it runs. Stop it when import is done.
sections.advanced:
### Import path
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[PC reads Square history] --> B[Write compressed monthly exports]
  B --> C[Serve manifest by QR or copy files]
  C --> D[Install files on this iPad]
  D --> E[Link SKU then barcode to Shopify catalogue]
  E --> F[Build report rollups and transaction records]
  F --> G[Read only history]
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| PC export | `tools/square-history/export.ts` |
| PC setup and use | `tools/square-history/README.md` |
| Import screen | `SquareHistorySettings` in `src/screens/SquareHistory.tsx` |
| Download, file copy and storage | `installFromUrl`, `installFromPicked`, `rebuild` in `src/lib/squareHistoryIO.ts` |
| SKU/barcode matching and rollups | `linkSale`, `addToRollups` in `src/lib/squareHistory.ts` |
| Transactions and reports display | `src/screens/Transactions.tsx`, `src/screens/Reports.tsx` |

The manifest is checked before file names are used. Each month is compressed separately so detailed history can be loaded without expanding the entire export at once.

pages.title: Taking payment
pages.summary: The Payment screen: the four ways to pay, part payments, what happens when the sale is paid, and what Back does once money has been taken.
pages.lead: The Payment screen is where a sale is paid for. You reach it with **Charge** on the cart (or **Take payment** in the guided checkout). Nothing is taken from the customer until they pay.

sections.basic:
### Getting there
Tap **Charge** on the cart. Two checks can come first, only if they apply:
1. A list of **price adjustments** on the sale, which you keep, change or remove. See [[sales/cart-and-prices]].
2. **Check these bundles**, if a bundle deal is not a recommended pair. See [[sales/bundles]].

Then the **Payment** screen opens.

### What you see
- The big number is **Total due**. Once part of the bill is paid it changes to **Remaining**, with *of $…* underneath.
- Under it, a list of the payments taken so far (card, cash, gift card) and what each paid.
- The ways to pay. In standard mode the buttons read **Card**, **Cash**, **Gift card** and **Split amount**. In Simple and Minimal modes they read **Pay by card**, **Pay with cash**, **Pay with a gift card** and **Split the payment**, each with a line under it saying what it does, and a heading *How is the customer paying?*
- If the card reader is not ready you see **Reader issue** in red at the top right. Cash and gift cards still work.

### The four ways to pay
- **Card**: the customer taps, inserts or swipes on the Zeller terminal. See [[pay/card]].
- **Cash**: a sheet opens where you tap the notes and coins the customer hands over. It works out the change and which notes and coins to give back. See [[pay/cash]], and [[cash]] for the drawer record behind it.
- **Gift card**: scan or type the gift card code. The amount taken is the card's balance, or what is still owed, whichever is less. The gift card is charged straight away. See [[pay/gift-card]].
- **Split amount** (**Split the payment**): take part of the bill one way and the rest another way, or divide it equally. Pick **Split equally 2**, **3** or **4**, or key in the first amount and tap **Continue**. The next payment then says *Next payment: $…*. The amount must be less than what remains. Tap **Cancel split** to go back to paying the lot. See [[pay/split-and-part]].

Every payment taken is added to the list. Pay the rest any way you like, in any order, until **Remaining** reaches $0.00.

### When it is fully paid
The sale finishes by itself the moment nothing remains. It is saved and sent to Shopify in the background, and the **Receipt** sheet opens: show a QR code, email or text the link, share it, or tap **No receipt**. Tapping that (or finishing the receipt) clears the cart for the next customer. See [[pay/receipts]].

If the total is $0.00 (a free sale), there is one button, **Complete $0.00 sale**.

### Going back
- **Nothing paid yet:** **Back** returns you to the cart and nothing has changed.
- **Part paid:** the cart is locked, so you cannot change items, clear it or save it. **Back** asks **Cancel this sale?**. If you choose **Refund & cancel**, card payments are refunded to the customer's card through the terminal. Cash and gift card payments are **not** returned automatically: hand the cash back yourself (the cash drawer record is put back for you) and deal with the gift card by hand.
- **While the terminal is working** there is no Back button. Use **Cancel** on the *Waiting on terminal* strip first.

### Good to know
- A cash payment can be rounded to the nearest 5c if **Cash rounding (5c)** is on in Settings ▸ Payments. It only changes the cash amount due, and only when cash pays the whole of what remains. Card amounts are always exact.
- The register will not lock, and staff cannot be switched, while a card payment is waiting on the terminal.
- If the iPad is offline the sale is kept on it and sent when it is back online. Card payments need a connection, so they will not work offline, but cash will.
sections.deep:
### Part payments and the order they are taken in
A sale is made of **payments** (the app calls them tenders). Each one has its own amount, and the sale is paid when they add up to the total. You can mix any methods, in any order, and as many as you like. The *Next payment* amount is just the figure the next card, cash or gift card payment will aim for: the split amount, an equal share, or everything that remains.

### Cash rounding in a part-paid sale
Rounding is worked out on the cash that is **due**, not on the amount handed over. If cash pays the whole of what remains, the due amount is rounded to the nearest 5c and the difference is kept on the payment. If cash is only part of the bill, nothing is rounded.

### The gift card is charged first, not last
When you choose a gift card, the amount is taken off the card's balance straight away, before the sale finishes. If Shopify cannot do it you see **Gift card could not be charged** with the reason, and nothing is added to the sale. This is why cancelling a part-paid sale does not give the money back to a gift card by itself.

### What "finished" means
When the last payment makes **Remaining** $0.00, the app builds the sale record, takes the sold units off the stock count on this iPad, puts the sale in a queue for Shopify, and, if the sale started from a saved cart, removes that saved cart. The queue creates the Shopify order and adjusts Shopify's stock. If that fails or the iPad is offline, the sale stays queued and is retried. You can see how many are waiting in More ▸ Support & diagnostics ▸ Sync.

### Why the cart locks
Once any payment is on the sale, changing the cart would make what was paid and what is owed disagree. So the lines, the keypad, Save cart and Clear cart all say **Payment in progress** until the sale is paid or cancelled.
sections.advanced:
### From Charge to a finished sale
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Charge in CartPane.tsx or Take payment in GuidedCheckout.tsx] --> B[Pay.tsx: remaining = total minus paidTotal]
  B --> C{which button}
  C -->|card| D[runCard: see the card page]
  C -->|cash| E[CashSheet then takeCash]
  C -->|gift card| F[GiftCheckSheet then useGift debits the card]
  C -->|split| G[chunk or equalLeft sets the next payment amount]
  D --> H[addTender adds to cart.tenders]
  E --> H
  F --> H
  G --> B
  H --> I{remaining is 0?}
  I -->|no| B
  I -->|yes| J[buildSale then applyLocalStock then recordSale]
  J --> K[ReceiptPrompt then finishAll empties the cart]
```

### Where the code is
| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| The screen and all its state | `Pay` in `src/screens/Pay.tsx` |
| Total, what is paid, what remains | `usePriced` in `src/state/selectors.ts` gives the total; `paidTotal` in `src/lib/saleBuilder.ts` adds up the payments; `Pay` itself works out what remains |
| Building a payment | `cardTender`, `cashTender` in `src/lib/saleBuilder.ts`; the gift card payment is built in `useGift` in `Pay.tsx` |
| Finishing | the `finalising` effect in `Pay.tsx`: `buildSale`, `applyLocalStock`, `recordSale` (`src/lib/saleBuilder.ts`, `src/lib/sync.ts`) |
| Cash ledger | `postCashSale`, `reverseCashTender`, `cashDue` in `src/lib/cashSale.ts` |
| Cancelling a part-paid sale | `abandon` in `Pay.tsx` |
| Which card states may use a sheet | `showsOwnSheet`, `showsWaitingStrip`, `lockPayButtons` in `src/lib/payUi.ts` |
| Simple mode wording | `payTitle`, `payHint`, `payQuestion` in `src/lib/simpleLabels.ts` |
| Receipt step | `ReceiptPrompt` in `src/screens/Receipt.tsx` |

The payments live on the cart as `cart.tenders`, so they survive leaving the screen and are what locks the cart. The sale's id (`cart.saleUuid`) is made at the first payment and kept until the sale is paid or cancelled. Card attempt references are built from it, which is how a payment can be matched to its sale later.

The finishing effect runs once (a `finalising` flag stops it repeating) when there is at least one payment, nothing remains, and the terminal is not waiting. The flag is only cleared by `finishAll`.

### Reading the code for a fault
- **Pay by card, Cash, Gift card and Split are all greyed out.** `lockPayButtons` is true while the card phase is waiting. If the app was closed mid-payment, reopen the Payment screen: the waiting state is not saved, but the attempt is. Check the card page for what happens to an unfinished attempt.
- **Paid in full but the sale did not finish.** The effect holds off while the card phase is `waiting`. Look for the strip at the top of the screen.
- **Cart is stuck as "Payment in progress" with nothing paid.** Something left a payment in `cart.tenders`. Open Payment and use **Back**, then **Refund & cancel**.
- **Sale is finished but missing in Shopify.** It is in the queue: More ▸ Support & diagnostics ▸ Sync shows how many are waiting and the last error, and **Sync now** retries.
- **A free sale has no payment buttons.** Expected: only **Complete $0.00 sale** shows, and it adds a $0 cash payment.
- **Tests.** `tests/payui.test.ts` (which card states may draw a sheet), `tests/sale.test.ts` and `tests/cashsale.test.ts` (building sales and cash payments), `tests/simplelabels.test.ts` (Simple mode wording).

pages.title: Paying by card
pages.summary: Taking a card payment on the Zeller terminal, what the strip and the sheets mean, and what to do when it is declined, not ready, or the result is unknown.
pages.lead: Card payments go through the Zeller terminal. The POS tells the terminal the amount, the customer pays on the terminal, and the result comes back to the Payment screen.

sections.basic:
### Taking a card payment
1. On the **Payment** screen tap **Card** (**Pay by card** in Simple and Minimal modes). The amount is shown on the button: it is what remains, or the next split amount.
2. A strip appears at the top: **Waiting on terminal · $…**, with a line saying what the terminal is doing. Zeller's own screen also appears on top while it works.
3. The customer taps, inserts or swipes their card, and enters their PIN or signs if the terminal asks.
4. When it is approved the payment is added to the list, and if nothing remains the sale finishes.

The line on the strip changes as it goes. You may see: *Tap, insert or swipe card on the terminal*, *Customer is choosing the card application* or *the account*, *Customer is entering their PIN*, *Waiting for signature*, *Signature cleared — sign again*, *Retrying — present the card again*, *Processing…*, and *Customer is choosing a tip*.

Wait for the result before touching anything else. While the terminal is working the other payment buttons are greyed out and there is no Back button, so a second charge cannot start by accident.

### Cancel
**Cancel** on the strip asks the terminal to stop. If the customer has not paid yet, the strip disappears and you can choose any payment method again. If the customer had already paid by the time you cancelled, the POS finds the payment and counts it, so you will not charge twice. If the customer cancels on the terminal itself, you are simply back at the payment buttons with nothing taken.

### Not approved
A sheet called **Not approved** says why in plain words, for example *Insufficient funds — try another card or split with another tender* or *Card expired. Try another card.* A number such as *Code 51* is the bank's code. **The cart is kept.** Choose:
- **Try card again**: starts a new card payment for the same amount.
- **Use another method**: closes the sheet so you can pay by cash, gift card or a split.

For more detail on responding safely to a decline, see [[fix/card-declined]].

A few messages mean the customer can fix it: *Incorrect PIN — try again*, *Please insert the card*, *Card read failed — tap, insert or swipe again*. Others mean the card cannot be used and they need another one. If the message says *contact Zeller*, the terminal's set-up needs attention and card payments will keep failing until Zeller fixes it. Take cash in the meantime.

### Payment status unknown
Sometimes the POS loses contact in the middle of a payment (the internet drops, the terminal times out) and cannot tell whether the customer was charged. A sheet called **Payment status unknown** opens and says *Checking…*.

**Do not charge the card again.** The customer may already have been charged. The POS asks Zeller about the payment by itself, up to six times, a few seconds apart. Usually it finds the answer:
- If it was approved, it is added to the sale as a card payment.
- If it was not, you see that the payment did not go through, and you can try again.

If it still cannot tell, the sheet stays and gives you four buttons:
- **Check again**: asks Zeller again.
- **Customer WAS charged**: only if you have **seen it approved on the terminal or the Zeller dashboard**. It records the payment as paid by card.
- **Customer was NOT charged**: only if you have checked and it is not there. It lets you charge again.
- **Close**: leaves the question open.

Both of the middle buttons ask you to confirm, and your name is saved with the decision. Until an unknown payment on this sale is settled, **Card** refuses with *A previous card payment has no result yet. Resolve it before charging again.* Cash and gift cards still work.

### Reader not ready
If the terminal cannot be used, a **Reader** sheet says what is wrong, with **Retry** and **Close**. The messages are:
- *Terminal not paired — open Diagnostics ▸ Zeller ▸ Setup.* The terminal has never been paired with this iPad (or the app was reinstalled).
- *No internet — card payments need a connection. Cash still works.*
- *Terminal is busy. Please wait and try again.* Or *The terminal is serving another register.*
- *Can’t reach the terminal — check its power and Wi‑Fi.* Or *Couldn’t connect to the terminal.*

If the reader is not ready you also see **Reader issue** in red at the top right of the Payment screen, and a **Reader issue** notice is added to your notifications.

To check or fix the reader, open **More ▸ Support & diagnostics**. Under **Zeller reader** you have **Check reader**, **Setup (pair terminal)**, and **Test purchase $1.00** with **Refund the $1.00 test** afterwards. After reinstalling the app you must pair the terminal again.

For a step-by-step reader troubleshooting guide, see [[fix/reader]].

### Good to know
- Card amounts are never rounded.
- A card payment can be refunded from the terminal if you cancel a part-paid sale (see [[pay]]).
- The register will not lock, and staff cannot be switched, while a card payment is waiting.
sections.deep:
### Why a card payment is never repeated by accident
Every card attempt gets its own reference, made from the sale's id and the attempt number. The POS saves the attempt on the iPad **before** it tells the terminal anything, then asks the terminal to take the payment. If the answer is ever unclear, it looks the payment up by that reference instead of guessing. That is how it can tell "the customer paid just as you pressed Cancel" from "nothing happened".

The same care explains the rule about unknown results: charging again before you know could take the money twice, so the POS blocks it until the first attempt is settled.

### What counts as "unknown"
The POS treats a result as unknown when it cannot be sure no money moved: the connection dropped after the terminal had started, the terminal timed out, the bank's answer could not be read, or a reversal was still pending. A plain decline before the card was processed is **not** unknown, and neither is a failure to start (no internet, not paired).

### The kinds of decline
Each bank or terminal code is put in one of four groups, and the message follows from the group:
- **Try another card**: insufficient funds, expired, lost or stolen, blocked, over the limit, not supported.
- **The customer can fix it**: wrong PIN, signature problem, card not read, card needs inserting.
- **Try again**: a bank, network or terminal hiccup.
- **Contact Zeller**: the merchant or terminal set-up is wrong. Retrying will not help.
A code the POS does not know shows the terminal's own wording, or *Declined (code …)*. The **Not approved** sheet always offers **Try card again**, whatever the group, so use the message to decide.

### Fees
Zeller's result does not include a fee, so the POS works one out. The rates are in **Settings ▸ Payments**: **Card-present fee %** (1.4% unless changed) and **Keyed / card-not-present fee %** (1.7%). A manually keyed or online-style payment uses the keyed rate. The fee is kept on the payment as an estimate. A refund does not return the original fee.

### Offline and the reader's state
The POS asks the terminal whether it is ready when the app starts, and again about every minute while it is not ready, so **Reader issue** clears by itself once the problem is fixed. A card payment needs the internet; cash and gift cards are separate, so cash always works.

### Cancelling a sale that already has a card payment
Choosing **Refund & cancel** on a part-paid sale refunds each card payment through the terminal, one after another. If a refund does not complete you see **Refund did not complete**, nothing is cancelled, and the problem is written to the history so you can follow it up. Check the terminal before trying again.
sections.advanced:
### What happens when you tap Card
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[runCard in Pay.tsx] --> B{buttons locked or an unknown attempt on this sale}
  B -->|unknown attempt| C[Payment status unknown sheet]
  B -->|no| D{terminal ready}
  D -->|no| E[checkReader in zellerBridge.tsx]
  E -->|still no| F[Reader sheet]
  D -->|yes| G[attemptRef then onStarted saves the attempt as started]
  E -->|ready| G
  G --> H[startCharge in zeller.ts calls terminal.purchase]
  H --> I[normalise turns the SDK result into a PaymentResult]
  I -->|APPROVED| J[cardTender then addTender]
  I -->|DECLINED| K[Not approved sheet]
  I -->|CANCELLED| L[back to idle]
  I -->|NOT_READY| F
  I -->|UNKNOWN| M[recheck: reconcile up to 6 times 4 s apart]
  M -->|approved| J
  M -->|declined or cancelled| K
  M -->|no answer| C
```

### Where the code is
| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| The flow, sheets and strip | `runCard`, `recheck`, `manualResolve` in `src/screens/Pay.tsx` |
| Which states may draw a sheet | `showsOwnSheet`, `showsWaitingStrip`, `lockPayButtons` in `src/lib/payUi.ts` |
| Talking to the SDK | `startCharge`, `startRefund`, `reconcile`, `normalise`, `describeEvent` in `src/lib/zeller.ts` |
| One terminal for the whole app | `ZellerRoot`, `getTerminal`, `checkReader`, `pairReader` in `src/zellerBridge.tsx` |
| Code to message | `RESPONSE_CODES`, `lookupResponse` in `src/lib/responseCodes.ts` |
| Fees | `feeFor`, `feeRateFor` in `src/lib/fees.ts`; `cardTender` in `src/lib/saleBuilder.ts` |
| Pairing, test purchase, attempts list | `src/screens/Diagnostics.tsx` |
| Saved attempts | `Attempt` in `src/state/store.ts` (`pos.attempts`) |
| Locking while waiting | `paymentActive` in `src/lib/screensaver.ts`, used by `lockDecision` in `src/lib/posLock.ts` and by staff switching in `src/lib/staffAuth.ts` |

The SDK returns errors instead of throwing them. `normalise` turns either kind of result into one of five outcomes: `APPROVED`, `DECLINED`, `CANCELLED`, `UNKNOWN` or `NOT_READY`, and nothing outside `zeller.ts` reads a raw SDK result. A network or connection failure is `NOT_READY` when the terminal had not started, and `UNKNOWN` once it had.

`startCharge` does one more thing before it returns. If the result is cancelled or unknown, or a decline arrived after the terminal had started processing, it calls `reconcile`, which looks the reference up with `getTransactions`. An approved match turns the result into `APPROVED`. That lookup is what makes Cancel safe.

The attempt's status moves `started`, then `approved`, `declined`, `cancelled`, `unknown` or `resolved`. A **started** attempt keeps `paymentActive` true for five minutes, which is what blocks locking and staff switching; an attempt left at **started** by a closed app stops blocking after that. The waiting state itself is not saved, so reopening Payment shows the buttons again, but an `unknown` attempt on the sale still blocks **Card** through `blockedByUnknown`.

Events are written to the history CSV with `csv.event`: `declined`, `cancelled`, `unknown_payment`, `unknown_resolved`, `refund_failed` and `void`.

### Reading the code for a fault
- **Card button does nothing.** The amount is $0 (`runCard` returns when it is 0 or less), the buttons are locked by a waiting card phase, or an `unknown` attempt exists for this sale.
- **"Reader issue" that will not clear.** In More ▸ Support & diagnostics tap **Check reader**: it calls `initialise` on the terminal. `Setup Required` means pair it. `Network Failure` shows as *Reader offline — no internet*.
- **The customer was charged but the sale shows no card payment.** It is an `unknown` attempt: check **Card attempts (this device)** in Support & diagnostics (the last eight, with their reference and who resolved them) and look for the same reference in the Zeller dashboard. The reference is the sale id followed by the attempt number.
- **A decline message is vague.** The code is not in `RESPONSE_CODES`, so the SDK's own text is shown. Add it there if you want better wording.
- **The reader says busy.** *Paired Device Busy* means another register is using the terminal. Only one register can charge at a time.
- **Tests.** `tests/lib.test.ts` covers the response codes, fees, `normalise`, and `startCharge` (approve; a cancel after processing that still approves through `reconcile`; a timeout that stays unknown; a decline that keeps the cart) and `startRefund`. `tests/payui.test.ts` covers which states may draw a sheet.

pages.title: Paying by cash
pages.summary: Taking cash by tapping the notes and coins handed over, giving change from the drawer, and what to do when the drawer cannot make the change.
pages.lead: Cash is taken by tapping the notes and coins the customer hands over. The POS works out the change, shows which notes and coins to take from the drawer, and keeps a record of what is in the drawer as it goes.

sections.basic:
### Taking cash
1. On the **Payment** screen tap **Cash** (**Pay with cash** in Simple and Minimal modes).
2. The **Cash received** sheet opens. At the top it shows **Due**, the amount the customer owes in cash.
3. Tap each note and coin the customer hands you. Each tap adds one. The number under the note or coin shows how many you have tapped, and **Received** shows the total.
4. The line under **Due** tells you where you are:
   - **Tap what the customer hands over**: nothing tapped yet.
   - **Short by $…** (red): they have not given enough.
   - **Exact** (green): the right amount.
   - **Change to give: $…** (green): they gave too much and you owe change. It turns red if the drawer cannot make that change (see below).

### The tap pad
- **Add / Remove** switch: choose **Remove** to take notes or coins off what you have tapped. Removing something you have not tapped says *None of that to remove.*
- **Each tap** (**×1**, **×5**, **×10**): how many one tap adds, handy for rolls of coins.
- **Undo** takes back your last tap and tells you what it removed and the new total. **Start over** clears everything.
- Notes are $100, $50, $20, $10 and $5. Coins are $2, $1, 50c, 20c, 10c and 5c.

### What happens next
- **Exact:** tap **Take cash**. The payment is added and, if nothing remains, the sale finishes.
- **Short:** you can ask for more, or tap **Take $… as part payment**. The cash is recorded as a payment of what they gave, and the rest is paid another way. See [[pay/split-and-part]].
- **Change to give:** tap **Next: give $… change**. The **Give change** screen shows **Take from the drawer** with the notes and coins to hand back.
  - **Gave this** confirms you handed over exactly that.
  - **I'll give different notes and coins** lets you tap what you really gave. The total must match the change owed.
  - **Show another way** appears only when Smart change is on in Settings ▸ Payments and there is more than one good option. It steps through them. See [[cash/smart-change]].
  - **Back** returns to the notes you tapped.

### When the drawer cannot make the change
A red box says **Can't make $… change** and **Next** is greyed out. See [[cash/change]] for what that means and how each option is found, or [[fix/cant-make-change]] for what to do at the till. It lists what could work:
- **Ask for less:** take a smaller part of what they handed over and give the rest straight back. Tap **Use that smaller handover** to do it.
- **Cash $… + the rest another way:** take part of the bill in cash (the most the drawer can make change for) and put the remainder on card or another method.
- **Or take the full amount by card.**

If the box says **No cash in the ledger**, the drawer was never opened or counted, so the POS has no idea what is in it. Open the drawer from More ▸ Cash drawer first. See [[cash/open-close]].

If you can see the drawer really does have the change and the record is out of date, tap **The drawer has it (ledger is out of date)**. You then tap the notes and coins you give. Fix the record later with **Correct contents** or **Count & close** in the cash drawer. See [[cash/open-close]].

### Skipping the tracking
Sometimes the queue is long and you just want to finish.
- **Exact amount (don't track notes)** shows before you tap anything. It takes the exact amount and does not touch the drawer record.
- **Done, but don't track it** on the **Give change** screen finishes the sale. The notes the customer handed over **are** added to the drawer record, but the change you gave is **not** taken out, so the record will show too much cash until the next count.

Every skip makes the record drift a little. A count and close at the end of the day puts it right.

### Cash rounding
If **Cash rounding (5c)** is on in Settings ▸ Payments, the cash due on the **last** payment is rounded to the nearest 5c. 1c and 2c round down, 3c and 4c round up. So $10.02 is due as $10.00 and $10.03 as $10.05. Earlier payments in a split are never rounded.

### Free sales
If the total is $0.00 the only button is **Complete $0.00 sale**.

### Cancelling a sale that has cash in it
If you back out of a part-paid sale, hand the cash back yourself. The drawer record is put back for you for any cash that was tracked.
sections.deep:
### Where the change comes from
The change is made from the notes and coins in the drawer record **plus what the customer just handed over**. So the customer's own notes can go straight back as change, and a drawer with no small notes can still change a $20 if the customer handed over a $10 and a $5 as well. Among all the exact ways to make the change, the POS picks the one with the fewest pieces, which is quickest to count out. With **Smart change** on it picks the way that leaves the drawer best stocked for the next sales instead (see [[cash/smart-change]]). The full story of how change is found is on [[cash/change]], and you can check a customer's notes before taking them with [[cash/check-change]].

### How rounding is worked out
Rounding is applied to the cash **due**, not to what was handed over, and only when that cash payment clears the whole of what remains. The sale keeps the real amount and records the rounding separately, so receipts and reports can show it. Rounding down means the customer paid up to 2c less than the bill, rounding up means up to 2c more. If the cash is only part of the bill, nothing is rounded.

### Short payments are not change
If the customer hands over less than is due, the payment is recorded as the amount handed over, with no change. That is what **Take $… as part payment** does.

### What each button writes to the drawer record
| You tap | Notes and coins in | Change out |
|---|---|---|
| **Take cash** (exact) | recorded | none |
| **Take $… as part payment** | recorded | none |
| **Gave this** | recorded | recorded |
| **Done, but don't track it** (change screen) | recorded | **not** recorded |
| **Exact amount (don't track notes)** | not recorded | not recorded |

### The two ways round a drawer that cannot make change
- **Ask for less** looks for the smallest amount you could keep from what they handed over that still covers the bill and whose change the drawer **can** make. Example: the drawer has one $5, the customer hands you $20, $10 and $5 for a $25 bill. Keep the $20 and $5 and hand the $10 straight back, so no change is needed at all.
- **Part in cash** looks for the largest cash amount below the bill, in 5c steps, whose change can be made. Example: the drawer has one $20, the customer hands you a $50 for a $37 bill. The $13 change cannot be made, but $30 in cash works ($20 change from the drawer), leaving $7 for card.

### The record can drift
The record is only as good as what is tapped. It lives on each iPad separately. See [[cash]]. Count & close, Correct contents, and the skip buttons above are the ways it gets reset or knocked out of line.
sections.advanced:
### From Cash to a payment
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Cash button in Pay.tsx] --> B[CashSheet receive step]
  B --> C{cashStatus of due and received}
  C -->|short| D[Take as part payment]
  C -->|exact| E[Take cash]
  C -->|change| F{planChange from drawer plus received}
  F -->|exact| G[GiveCash change step]
  F -->|impossible| H[handBackOptions and partCashOption]
  H --> G
  G --> I[onTake with received and given]
  D --> I
  E --> I
  I --> J[takeCash in Pay.tsx]
  J --> K[cashTender builds the Tender]
  J --> L[postCashSale writes the ledger]
  K --> M[addTender]
```

### Where the code is
| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| The sheet and its two steps | `CashSheet` in `src/screens/CashSheet.tsx` |
| The change step (also used for cash refunds) | `GiveCash`, `GiveCashSheet` in `src/screens/CashSheet.tsx` |
| The tap pad | `DenomPad` in `src/ui/DenomPad.tsx`; the maths in `src/lib/cashLedger.ts` |
| Due, short, exact, change | `cashDue`, `cashStatus` in `src/lib/cashSale.ts` |
| Which notes and coins to give | `planChange` in `src/lib/cashSale.ts`; `planChangeSmart` in `src/lib/changeScore.ts` when Smart change is on |
| Ask for less, part in cash | `handBackOptions`, `partCashOption` in `src/lib/cashSale.ts` |
| Building the payment | `cashTender` in `src/lib/saleBuilder.ts`; `takeCash` in `src/screens/Pay.tsx` |
| Writing and undoing the drawer record | `postCashSale`, `reverseCashTender` in `src/lib/cashSale.ts` |
| Rounding | `roundCash` in `src/lib/money.ts` |
| Empty drawer check | `ledgerEmpty` in `src/lib/cashSale.ts` |

### The payment record
A cash payment (a `Tender` of kind `cash`) has these fields:
- `amountCents`: what was applied to the bill. For a settling payment this is the amount due **before** rounding. For a short payment it is what was handed over.
- `tenderedCents` and `changeCents`: what was handed over and what went back.
- `roundingCents`: the rounded due minus the amount (can be negative).
- `cashIn` and `cashOut`: the notes and coins received and given, only when they were tracked.

`cashTender` settles when the amount handed over is at least the due amount (rounded if rounding is on). Rounding is only passed in when `takeCash` sees `isFinal`: the payment is for everything that remains and it is not a part-cash amount (`applyCents` is not set). The sheet shows the same rounded amount because it gets it from `cashDue`.

`takeCash` writes to the drawer record only when `received` or `given` is set, which is why the skip buttons behave as the table above says. On a cancelled sale `reverseCashTender` takes out `cashIn` and puts back `cashOut`.

### Reading the code for a fault
- **Next is greyed out and the box says Can't make change.** `planChange` found no exact combination from the drawer plus what was received. Check the record in More ▸ Cash drawer.
- **The drawer record shows more cash than the drawer holds.** Someone used **Done, but don't track it** on the change screen, or gave change without confirming. Use Correct contents.
- **Rounded amount looks wrong.** Check Settings ▸ Payments ▸ Cash rounding (5c). It only applies when this payment clears the remaining amount.
- **Show another way is missing.** Smart change is off, there is only one way to make the change, or the search was cut short.
