You cannot save an empty cart ("Cart is empty"), or a cart that has had part of its payment taken ("Payment in progress").

### Finding and opening one
Open **More ▸ Saved carts**, or tap the **Saved carts** tile on the Quick Menu. Each row shows the name, how many items, the total, the customer, and any note. You can also type a name, note or customer in the Checkout search box and pick the **Saved carts** filter.

Tap a cart to see what is in it, then:
- **Open**: if your cart is empty the saved cart goes straight in. If it already has items you are asked **Merge Carts?**, and choosing **Merge** adds the saved items to what is already there.
- **Assign → name**: marks the cart as meant for that staff member. Their name appears on the row. It is a label only: anyone can still open it.
- **Delete**: asks "Delete saved cart?" first. It is removed from every register.

On the list you can also **swipe a row** to delete it. You are asked to confirm, and the row slides back if you say no.

### Good to know
- Opening a saved cart does not use it up. It stays in the list until the sale made from it is paid, then it is removed for you.
- A **whole order price** is not kept in a saved cart. The Save cart sheet warns you, and the cart comes back at its normal total.
- A row that says **not synced** has not reached the other registers yet. It sends as soon as the register is online.
sections.deep:
### How carts are shared
Saved carts are kept in your Shopify store, so any register can open them. A register sends its changes straight away, and every register checks for new or changed carts about every 25 seconds while the app is open. The cart you saved a moment ago may take up to that long to appear on another register.

If a register is offline, the cart is kept on that register (marked **not synced**) and sent when the connection returns. Until then, that register's copy wins over anything newer that arrives for the same cart, so your own unsent change is never overwritten.

### Deleting
Deleting marks the cart as void. Other registers drop it at their next check. There is no "undo", and nothing is asked a second time on the other registers.

### Open into an empty cart, or merge
- **Empty cart:** the saved items, customer and cart discount replace it. Any half-made payment details are cleared, so a saved cart can never bring a payment with it.
- **Cart with items:** the saved lines are added. If **Consolidate identical items** is on, the same item combines into one line, except lines that have been changed (a changed price, a discount, a note or an adjustment), which stay separate. Your current cart's customer and discount are kept, and the saved cart's are used only if the current cart has none. If any line in the merged cart has a price adjustment, the whole order price is dropped.

### Two registers, one cart
There is no lock on a saved cart. If two registers change the same one at nearly the same moment, the one that sends last wins. For a shop with a few registers this is rare, but it is a good reason to **Open** a cart rather than edit it in two places.
sections.advanced:
### From Save cart to another register
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Save cart sheet: SaveCartSheet in sheets.tsx] --> B[saveCartLocal in sync.ts: dirty true]
  B --> C[pushSaved: meta.upsert to pos_saved_cart]
  C -->|sent| D[dirty false, remoteId and version stored]
  C -->|offline| E[stays dirty, App.tsx 25 s tick retries]
  F[pollShared every 25 s] --> G[pullSaved: meta.list first 100]
  G -->|local copy dirty| H[keep local]
  G -->|status void| I[remove locally]
  G -->|open| J[replace or add local copy]
  K[Open: openSavedCart in savedOps.ts] --> L{current cart empty?}
  L -->|yes| M[setCart with savedFrom set]
  L -->|no| N[confirm Merge Carts then mergeCarts in cartOps.ts]
  M --> O[Pay.tsx on a paid sale: updateSaved savedFrom void]
```

### Where the code is
| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Save sheet (clears the cart after saving) | `SaveCartSheet` in `src/screens/sheets.tsx`; its `onSaved` empties the cart in `CartPane.tsx` and `GuidedCheckout.tsx` |
| The list, Open, Assign, Delete, swipe | `src/screens/SavedCarts.tsx` (`SavedCarts`, `SwipeRow` in `src/ui/SwipeRow.tsx`) |
| Open, delete, assign | `openSavedCart`, `deleteSavedCart`, `assignSavedCart` in `src/lib/savedOps.ts` |
| Saving and syncing | `saveCartLocal`, `updateSaved`, `pushSaved`, `pullSaved`, `cartFields` in `src/lib/sync.ts` |
| The stored shape | `SavedCart` in `src/state/store.ts`; the `pos_saved_cart` definition in `src/lib/shopify/metaobjects.ts` (`ensureDefinitions`) |
| Merging | `mergeCarts` in `src/lib/cartOps.ts` |
| Removing a used cart | the `savedFrom` check in `Pay.tsx` |
| Search filter | the `carts` results in `Checkout.tsx` |
| The 25 second tick | `App.tsx` (`pollShared`, `pushSaved`) |

A saved cart stores `lines_json`, `discount_json` and `customer_json` along with the name, note, employee, register and a `version`. `SaveCartSheet` strips the cart's own name and `orderAdjust` before saving, which is why a whole order price does not survive. Assigning writes the status as `assigned:` followed by the staff id, and `pullSaved` reads it back. Nothing else reads that field.

`pullSaved` asks for up to 100 carts. A cart that is deleted elsewhere and is not in that list is left alone, because the code does not guess about deletions. The `locked_by` and `locked_at` fields exist in the Shopify definition but nothing writes them yet.

### Reading the code for a fault
- **A cart saved on one register is missing on another.** On the saving register, look for **not synced**: it is still `dirty`. Otherwise check the other register's sync strip, and that Settings ▸ Shopify ▸ **Set up shared storage (metaobjects)** was run (it creates `pos_saved_cart`).
- **A deleted cart came back.** The register that still had it was offline with its own copy marked dirty, and sent it on reconnecting.
- **Saved, but the whole order price is gone.** Working as designed (see `SaveCartSheet`).
- **A saved cart is still listed after the sale was paid.** The sale was made from a merged cart, not an opened one: only `openSavedCart` into an empty cart sets `savedFrom`. Delete the saved cart by hand.
- **Merge made two lines of the same item.** One had a changed price, discount, note or adjustment, so `mergeCarts` keeps them apart.
- **Tests.** There is no test for the saved cart sync itself. `mergeCarts` is covered in `tests/itemadjust.test.ts` and `tests/lineadjust.test.ts`.

pages.title: Scanning items, passes and gift cards
pages.summary: The Bluetooth scanner and the camera, what a scan does on each screen, and what to do when scanning misbehaves.
pages.lead: A scan is the quickest way to add an item. The POS understands three kinds of code: item barcodes, cashier passes and gift card QR codes.

sections.basic:
### The two scanners
- **Bluetooth scanner.** Pair it in the iPad's own Settings as a keyboard (HID mode). After that, on Checkout, just scan: the item goes in the cart.
- **Camera.** Tap the camera icon next to the search bar. A full-screen camera opens and stays open, so you can scan several things in a row. Each scan shows a green message ("Added Dragon plush") or a red one ("Not found: …"). Tap **Done** when finished. The camera reads EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A, UPC-E, Code 128, Code 39, ITF-14 and QR codes.

The gift card pop-up (Charge ▸ Gift card) has its own camera button for scanning a gift card's QR code.

To check a Bluetooth scanner is working, go to Settings ▸ **Hardware** and scan something. The last few scans are listed and nothing is added to any cart. See [[settings/hardware]] for the test steps.

### What a scan does, by screen
| Where you are | Item barcode | Cashier pass | Gift card QR |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Checkout** | Adds 1 to the cart | Signs that person in; the cart stays as it is | Tells you to redeem it from Charge ▸ Gift card |
| **Price check / Stock check** | Shows its price or stock; the cart is not touched | "That is a cashier pass, not an item." | Tells you to check it from Charge ▸ Gift card |
| **Staff sign-in** | Not accepted | Signs in | Not accepted |

If nothing matches you see **No item for** followed by the code. Fix that in Shopify (see Advanced for the usual causes).

### When scanning does nothing
- A pop-up is open, or you are on another screen (such as Pay). Scanning only adds to the cart from the Checkout screen with nothing on top of it.
- You were typing in a box a moment ago. Scans are ignored for about 2½ seconds after you finish typing, so the scanner cannot take over what you were typing.
- The scanner is not paired or not in keyboard mode. Test it in Settings ▸ Hardware.

### Getting the on-screen keyboard back
A Bluetooth scanner stops the iPad showing its on-screen keyboard. On the POS-mate scanner, **double-click the scanner button** to show the keyboard, and double-click again to hide it.
sections.deep:
### How a code is matched
The code is compared with each variation's **barcode** after removing spaces and any zeros at the start. That is why a 12-digit UPC and the 13-digit EAN that begins with 0 find the same item. If no barcode matches, the code is tried against each **SKU** exactly, ignoring capital letters. If two items share a barcode, the first one found wins, so keep barcodes unique.

### The order things are checked
Checkout asks "is it a cashier pass?" first, then "is it an item?", then "is it a gift card?". The Price check and Stock check pop-ups ask "is it an item?" first, so a real barcode always wins there. A pass is the letter P followed by 12 letters and digits. A gift card QR starts with `shopify-giftcard-v1-`. Because no item should ever look like either, the order rarely matters.

### Why a scanner acts like a keyboard
A Bluetooth scanner connected this way pretends to be a keyboard: it types the digits and then presses Return. The POS keeps a hidden, always-ready text box that catches those keystrokes, and treats Return as "scan finished". This is also why a scanner can fight with a real keyboard, and why the POS backs off while you type.

### Two scans of the same code
The camera ignores the same code if it is seen again within about a second, so holding the camera on one barcode does not add ten.
sections.advanced:
### The path of a scan
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  K[Scanner types code and Return] --> H[HidScanner hidden TextInput]
  H -->|onSubmitEditing| S[onScan code]
  C[CameraScanner onBarcodeScanned] -->|same code within 1.2 s ignored| S
  S --> B{Checkout: isBadgeCode?}
  B -->|yes| P[signInWithPass, cart unchanged]
  B -->|no| F[findByBarcode: barcode then SKU]
  F -->|found| A[add 1, toast Added]
  F -->|not found| G{isGiftQr?}
  G -->|yes| M[toast: redeem from Charge]
  G -->|no| N[toast: No item for code]
```

### Where the code is
| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Hidden keyboard capture, camera screen | `src/screens/Scanner.tsx` (`HidScanner`, `CameraScanner`) |
| When Checkout listens | `Checkout.tsx`: `HidScanner enabled={active && nav.tab === 'checkout' && sheet === 'none' && !cam && nav.stack.length === 0}` |
| Matching | `findByBarcode`, `normaliseBarcode` in `src/lib/cartOps.ts` (strips whitespace and leading zeros; then SKU, lower-cased) |
| Pass, gift, none | `resolveScan`, `scanProblem` in `src/lib/lookup.ts`; `isBadgeCode`, `cleanScan`, `BADGE_RE` (`/^P[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{12}$/`) in `src/lib/badge.ts`; `isGiftQr` in `src/lib/giftCode.ts` |
| Not stealing the keyboard | `src/lib/focusGuard.ts` (`isUserTyping`, `TYPING_GRACE_MS` = 2500); every `Field` calls `fieldFocused` and `fieldBlurred` |
| Price and Stock check | `src/screens/Lookup.tsx` (`HidScanner enabled={visible && !cam}`) |
| Sign-in screen | `src/screens/StaffLogin.tsx` (only passes accepted) |
| Hardware test | `HardwareTest` in `Settings.tsx` (keeps the last 8 scans) |
| Tests | `tests/focusguard.test.ts`, `tests/lookup.test.ts` |

### How HidScanner keeps focus
It only takes focus when `isUserTyping()` is false and `Keyboard.isVisible()` is false. It tries on mount and then every 1.5 seconds if it has lost focus. The text box is 1 pixel, almost invisible, hides the soft keyboard (`showSoftInputOnFocus={false}`), and is replaced (new `key`) after every scan so the old text can never leak into the next code. The code used is `nativeEvent.text`, falling back to the last typed value, trimmed.

### Reading the code for a fault
- **"No item for …" on a real product.** The variation has no `barcode` or `sku` on this device, or the value differs by more than spaces and leading zeros. A Shopify barcode with letters or a dash will not match a scan without them. Fix it in Shopify, then import again in Settings ▸ Shopify.
- **Scan works in Settings ▸ Hardware but not on Checkout.** One of the five conditions in the `enabled` expression is false: a sheet is open, the camera is up, a screen is stacked on top, or the tab is not Checkout.
- **Scan is ignored just after typing.** Working as designed (`TYPING_GRACE_MS`). Wait about 2½ seconds.
- **The keyboard disappears while typing.** That was a bug fixed in patch 0001; if it returns, check that the input in question is a kit `Field` (a raw `TextInput` is invisible to the guard, though `Keyboard.isVisible()` still covers it).
- **The same item is added twice.** The scanner sent the code twice, or its trigger was held. The camera path de-duplicates within 1.2 seconds; the Bluetooth path does not.
- **Characters come out wrong.** The scanner's keyboard layout does not match the iPad's. Change it with the scanner's setup barcodes, not in the app.

pages.title: Variations, stock counts and negative stock
pages.summary: Choosing a variation, what the stock dots and words mean, why you can sell below zero, and how counts stay up to date.
pages.lead: A product can come in several variations, such as colour or size. Each variation has its own price and its own stock count.

sections.basic:
### Choosing a variation
Tap a product that has more than one variation and the grid is replaced by one tile per variation. Each shows its photo, name, price and stock. Tap the one you want and it goes in the cart, and you are back where you were. The bar above shows the product as the last step, for example *Home > Dragons > Highland cow*, so tap an earlier name to leave without choosing.

A product with only one variation skips this step and is added straight away.

### What the stock words mean
| You see | It means |
|---|---|
| **12 in stock** | There are 12 counted. |
| **Out of stock** | The count is 0. |
| **3 oversold** | The count is below zero: 3 more have been sold than were counted. |
| **Not tracked** | This item has no stock count (a service, or tracking is off in Shopify). |

The coloured dot follows the same idea: green is fine, amber is 2 or fewer (including 0), and red is oversold.

### Selling when stock is 0
You can always sell an item that shows 0 or below. The POS warns you ("stock will go negative") and carries on, because the shelf is the truth and the count may simply be behind.

### When the count changes
- Selling an item lowers its count straight away on this device.
- A refund puts it back.
- Counts also change when someone on another register or in Shopify changes them. The app checks about every 25 seconds while it is open.
- If any item goes below zero, a notification appears in the Notifications tab that takes you to Inventory so you can fix the count.

### Fixing a wrong count
Counts are corrected in Inventory (set a count, receive stock, or adjust it). If many items look wrong after a busy day, check that sales are not queued: the strip on Checkout says "Offline" or "queued" when they are.
sections.deep:
### Why overselling is allowed
Shopify is told to take the stock off even if that makes it negative. A till that refused to sell would stop a customer who is standing there with the item in their hand, so the rule is: sell first, correct the count after.

### Not tracked
A variation whose stock is "not tracked" never shows a dot, is never counted in totals, and is not changed by sales or refunds. This is not the same as 0.

### Stock check totals
The Stock check tile shows the scanned variation first, then its siblings, and a total. The total only adds counts that are tracked, and treats negative counts as 0, so oversold stock does not pull the total down. It also says how many variations are not tracked, in brackets after the total.

### Several registers
Each register keeps its own copy of the counts and applies its own sales at once, so the number you see is right for you immediately. The real number lives in Shopify and each register catches up every 25 seconds or so. Two registers selling the last item at the same moment will both succeed, and the count will go to -1.
sections.advanced:
### Data and thresholds
`Variant.stock` is `number | null` (`null` = not tracked). The thresholds are in two places that agree: `stockToneOf` in `src/lib/lookup.ts` (`none`, `ok`, `low` at 1 to 2, `out` at 0, `neg` below 0) and `stockTone` in `src/state/selectors.ts` for the tile dot (which has no separate `out`, so 0 shows as low).

### When stock moves
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Add an item] --> B{stock tracked and stock minus qty below 0?}
  B -->|yes| W[toast: stock will go negative]
  B -->|no| T[toast: Added item]
  S[Sale completes] --> L[applyLocalStock: sync.ts]
  L --> O[outbox: Shopify orderCreate with DECREMENT_IGNORING_POLICY]
  O --> H[Shopify lowers the stock]
  P[pollShared every 25 s] --> D[fetchStockDelta since stockSince]
  D --> U[variants stock replaced from Shopify]
```

- `applyLocalStock` changes the local count for each sold line by `-qty` for a sale, `+qty` for a refund, skipping untracked variations.
- Shopify's own count is lowered by the order itself (`DECREMENT_IGNORING_POLICY`), so the POS does not send a second adjustment for sales.
- For refunds the outbox item carries `done: { order, stock }` and the stock step uses `adjustStock` in `src/lib/shopify/inventory.ts` (`inventoryAdjustQuantities` with an idempotency key, so a retry cannot apply twice).
- `pollShared` fetches stock changes since `stockSince` and replaces the matching variants' counts. Remote values win, which is how the count is corrected after a manual change in Shopify.
- `App.tsx` runs a 25-second tick that polls, empties the outbox, and raises the "N item(s) with negative stock" notice (route `inventory`).

### The picker
`VariantPicker` in `Tiles.tsx` draws one tile per variation using `pickerVariants` (catalogue order, no duplicate ids) and `stockText`. It is a level of the grid, not a popup: `pickerCrumbs` adds the product as the last crumb, and changing tab, page, path or edit mode closes it (the `useEffect` that calls `setVariants(null)` in `Checkout.tsx`).

### Reading the code for a fault
- **Count did not drop after a sale.** The variation is untracked (`stock === null`), or `inventoryItemId` is missing so a later `pollShared` cannot match it. Check the variant on the device.
- **Count jumped back after a sale.** `pollShared` replaced it with Shopify's number; the order has probably not reached Shopify yet (outbox not empty).
- **Stock dot differs from the picker word.** Expected at exactly 0: the tile dot is amber for low, the picker says Out of stock.
- **Tests.** `tests/lookup.test.ts` covers the tones, the words, the stock check totals and the picker helpers.

pages.title: Settings
pages.summary: Find Shopify, payment, hardware, data, receipt, backup, display and other register settings.
pages.lead: Open **More ▸ Settings** to configure Shopify, payments, discounts, hardware and this register. Tap a section to open it; use the back button to return to the Settings list.

sections.basic:
### Find a setting
- **Shopify** connects the register to your shop; see [[settings/shopify]].
- **Payments** contains cash rounding, Smart change and card fee estimates; see [[settings/payments]].
- **Discounts & bundles** manages the bundle deals used in Checkout.
- **Hardware** opens the scanner test; see [[settings/hardware]].
- **Data** exports CSV files or deletes local history.
- **Square history** imports old Square sales for Reports.
- **Grid import / export** moves the Checkout tile layout.
- **Gift cards** has the claim-page and cashier-pass server settings.
- **Receipts** configures receipt and tax-invoice details; see [[settings/receipts]].
- **Backup & transfer** moves settings and logins to another device; **Data** exports or deletes local CSV history. See [[settings/backup]].
- **Screensaver & display** controls this iPad's idle screen and Keep iPad awake; see [[staff/screensaver]].
- **Theme** changes the app's appearance; see [[settings/theme]]. **About** shows app information.

The Settings list also has Checkout options for consolidating identical items and the tax display. Managers and Owners can access Settings when staff sign-in is required; cashiers cannot.
sections.deep:
### Settings are not all shared the same way
Some choices apply only to this register, such as Smart change and Screensaver & display. Shared settings, such as staff and bundle deals, sync with the other registers. The screen or setting guide explains when a choice is local.

The Payments section shows fee rates used for estimates. Zeller does not report actual card fees to the POS, and the automatic cash tender machine is still under construction; cash is entered and given by hand.
sections.advanced:
### Settings sections
| Section | Component or route |
|---|---|
| Settings list and section navigation | `src/screens/Settings.tsx` |
| Shopify connection and catalogue import | `ShopifySettings` in `src/screens/Settings.tsx` |
| Payments, fees and cash rounding | Payments section in `src/screens/Settings.tsx` |
| Bundle deals | `BundlesEditor` in `src/screens/BundleBuilder.tsx` |
| Hardware scanner test | `HardwareTest` in `src/screens/Settings.tsx` |
| Screensaver and display | `DisplaySettings` in `src/screens/Settings.tsx` |
| Settings model and defaults | `src/state/store.ts` |

Each section is a panel within the Settings screen. Its values may be stored locally, shared with the other registers, or held in the iPad's secure storage depending on the setting.

pages.title: Backup, transfer and local data
pages.summary: Export and restore settings securely, move them to another iPad, or export and delete local CSV history.
pages.lead: Use **More ▸ Settings ▸ Backup & transfer** to move settings and logins to another iPad. Use **More ▸ Settings ▸ Data** to export or delete this iPad's local CSV history; these are separate tools.

sections.basic:
### Create a backup
1. In **Backup & transfer**, enter a passphrase of at least **8 characters** in **Passphrase** and **Repeat passphrase**.
2. Tap **Export encrypted backup**, then save or share the file somewhere safe.
3. Keep the passphrase separate and safe. It is needed to open the encrypted backup.

The encrypted backup includes settings, staff, the grid layout and logins. It does not include sales history or the product catalogue. Zeller reader pairing stays on the original iPad.

**Export plain JSON (not encrypted)** is available only after a warning and confirmation. The file contains Shopify and other login secrets in readable text. Prefer the encrypted backup; if you export plain JSON, protect it and delete it after importing.

### Restore on another iPad
Tap **Choose backup file…** and select the backup. For an encrypted file, enter its passphrase and tap **Decrypt & restore**. Confirm the restore. It replaces the receiving iPad's settings, grid and logins, but keeps that iPad's own register name and ID.

After restoring, open **Settings ▸ Shopify** and tap **Import from Shopify** to reload the catalogue. Pair the Zeller reader again on the receiving device.

### Export or delete CSV history
Open **Settings ▸ Data**. **Export CSV** shares the local history files. Every sale, refund and declined card attempt is kept on this device and the files are not auto-cleared.

**Delete local history** asks twice before erasing the CSV files from this iPad. Export first if you need them. Deleting these local files does not delete the orders in Shopify.
sections.deep:
### What is and is not transferred
The backup carries settings, staff, the Checkout grid and configured logins such as Shopify, receipt and pass-server credentials. Sales history and the imported catalogue are not in the backup; Shopify remains the source to import them again. The Zeller reader pairing, register name and register ID belong to the receiving device and are not overwritten.

An encrypted file cannot be opened without its passphrase. A plain JSON backup includes secrets and should be treated like a password file. Uploaded screensaver logos can be included in the backup; the device-specific local file path is not copied.

### Local CSV history
The CSV files are separate from Shopify orders and the backup. They stay in the app's files on this iPad until you share or delete them. Deleting the local files cannot be undone from this screen.
sections.advanced:
### Backup and restore path
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Collect settings grid and credentials] --> B[Encrypt with passphrase or export plain JSON]
  B --> C[Share backup file]
  C --> D[Choose file on receiving iPad]
  D --> E[Decrypt when needed and confirm restore]
```

pages.title: Hardware and the scanner test
pages.summary: Pair a Bluetooth scanner as an HID keyboard, test it in Settings and check what the scanner returns.
pages.lead: Use **More ▸ Settings ▸ Hardware** to test a Bluetooth scanner without changing the cart. Pair the scanner in the iPad's Bluetooth settings in **HID keyboard** mode first.

sections.basic:
### Test a scanner
1. Pair the Bluetooth scanner with the iPad as a keyboard in HID mode.
2. Open **More ▸ Settings ▸ Hardware**.
3. Scan a barcode. The scanner test lists the last few codes it received.

The test shows the raw scanned text. It does not look up an item and does not add anything to a cart. For the camera scanner, item lookup and common scan problems, see [[sales/scanners]].

### If the scan does not appear
Check that the scanner is connected to this iPad and configured as a keyboard (HID). Return to **Hardware** and scan again. If it appears in the test but not on Checkout, use the scanner guide to check the screen and input rules: [[sales/scanners]].
sections.deep:
### How the HID test works
A Bluetooth HID scanner sends the barcode as keyboard input and finishes it with Return. The POS catches that text in a hidden input field; the Hardware test then shows the complete scanned value. Because this screen only records scans, it can confirm what the scanner sent without depending on a product's barcode or SKU being correct.
sections.advanced:
### Test input path
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Pair scanner as HID keyboard] --> B[Open Hardware test]
  B --> C[Scanner types code and Return]
  C --> D[Show raw code in recent scans]
  D --> E[Cart and catalogue stay unchanged]
```

| Bluetooth HID input | `HidScanner` in `src/screens/Scanner.tsx` |

The Hardware test keeps the most recent eight scans in memory while it is open. It does not save those scan values to the catalogue or sales history.

pages.title: Payment settings
pages.summary: Set cash rounding, Smart change and estimated card fee rates, and open Zeller reader setup.
pages.lead: Open **More ▸ Settings ▸ Payments** to choose cash rounding, Smart change and the fee rates used in POS estimates. Reader setup is in **Support & diagnostics**.

sections.basic:
### Cash rounding
**Cash rounding (5c)** rounds the amount due in cash to the nearest five cents. It applies to the cash amount only; card payments are not rounded by this setting. The setting is on by default.

### Smart change
Turn on **Smart change** to choose notes and coins that leave the drawer better stocked for later sales. It applies to this register only. For how the choice is calculated, see [[cash/smart-change]].

### Card fee rates and the terminal
Set **Card-present fee %** and **Keyed / card-not-present fee %** to match the rates you use. They are estimates for reports; the Zeller SDK does not return the actual fee. A card refund does not return the original fee.

To pair or check the reader, tap **Reader & pairing**. In **Support & diagnostics**, use **Setup (pair terminal)**. Card payments need a network connection and a paired terminal. The **Automatic cash tender machine** option is still under construction and disabled; cash notes and coins are handled by hand.
sections.deep:
### What each choice affects
- Cash rounding applies to the amount due on a cash tender, not card or gift-card amounts.
- Smart change is a per-register preference and works with the drawer's note-and-coin counts and sales history.
- Card fee rates are stored as shared settings and are used to estimate fees. Changing a rate does not change the amount charged by Zeller.
- Reader pairing is device-specific. If you reinstall the app, pair the terminal again.

The default estimates are **1.4%** for card-present and **1.7%** for keyed/card-not-present. Adjust them if your actual rate differs.
sections.advanced:
### Payment settings and reader path
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Choose rounding or fee estimates] --> B[Save payment settings]
  C[Open Reader and pairing] --> D[Support and diagnostics]
  D --> E[Setup pair terminal]
  E --> F[Check reader before taking card payment]
```

| Zeller payment request and results | `src/lib/zeller.ts`, `src/screens/Pay.tsx` |

The fee estimates are recorded with sales for reporting; they are not a quote from the terminal. The Settings footer explains that actual card fees are not provided by the Zeller SDK.

pages.title: Receipt settings
pages.summary: Configure the receipt page, business details, ABN, return policy and GST tax invoices.
pages.lead: Open **More ▸ Settings ▸ Receipts** to add your business details to receipts and connect the receipt page that customers open from a QR code or link.

sections.basic:
### Enter business details
Fill in **Business / trading name**, **ABN**, **Address**, **Phone**, **Email** and **Website** as needed. Add a **Return policy (optional)** if you want it printed. When the business name is blank, the receipt uses your Shopify shop name.

These details are copied into each receipt when it is made. Changing them later does not rewrite receipts that have already been issued.

### Connect and test the receipt page
Enter the **Receipt server URL** and **Receipt server secret (RECEIPT_SECRET)** supplied for your receipt server. Tap **Send test receipt** to upload a sample and open its page. The server must be deployed and configured before the link can work.

When a receipt page is configured, the customer can scan a QR or open a link to see the receipt and download it. For the customer-facing Receipt sheet and receipt page, see [[pay/receipts]].

### GST tax invoices
Turn on **Registered for GST** only if your business is registered. Receipts are then titled **Tax invoice** and show the GST included in the total. Prices are treated as GST-inclusive; gift-card lines are excluded from the GST calculation.
sections.deep:
### What appears on the receipt
The seller name, ABN and contact details, return policy, receipt and order information, items, payments and totals are captured in the receipt snapshot. The GST amount is calculated as one-eleventh of the GST-inclusive total for non-gift-card lines. The Receipt server renders the uploaded snapshot as a page with PDF and image download.

Use the test button to check that the URL and server secret work together. If it fails, confirm the Worker is deployed and that the URL and `RECEIPT_SECRET` match its configuration.
sections.advanced:
### Receipt publishing path
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Enter receipt server URL and secret] --> B[Make sample receipt]
  B --> C[Upload snapshot to receipt server]
  C --> D[Open customer receipt page]
  E[Save seller and GST details] --> F[Copy details into each new receipt]
```

pages.title: Connecting Shopify
pages.summary: Enter the shop domain and app credentials, test the connection, choose a location and import the catalogue.
pages.lead: Open **More ▸ Settings ▸ Shopify** to connect the register to a Shopify store, choose the stock location and import its catalogue.

sections.basic:
### Connect a shop
1. Enter the **Store domain**, **Client ID (Dev Dashboard app)** and **Client secret**.
2. Tap **Save & test connection**. The register checks the credentials with Shopify and shows the shop name and reported scopes if successful.
3. Choose a **Location (stock & orders)** if more than one active location is available.
4. Tap **Import from Shopify** to load variants, collections, customers and discounts.

The domain can be entered as `yourshop.myshopify.com`; the screen normalises it. The Client ID and Client secret are from your Shopify Dev Dashboard app. They are stored in the iOS Keychain on this iPad, not shared with the other registers.

### Shared storage and disconnecting
If you use multiple registers, tap **Set up shared storage (metaobjects)** to prepare the Shopify metaobjects used for shared POS data. **Disconnect** removes the Shopify credentials from this iPad; the existing local catalogue remains until you import again.
sections.deep:
### Which location is used
The selected active Shopify location is used for stock and orders. When Shopify reports a single active location and none has been saved yet, the register selects it automatically. With multiple active locations, choose the one this register should use.

The import button refreshes product variants, collections, customers and discounts from Shopify. The connected shop name and local catalogue counts appear on the Shopify settings screen.

### If the connection fails
Check the shop domain and the Client ID and Client secret for the Dev Dashboard app, then use **Save & test connection** again. A successful connection displays a message naming the shop. If it connects but the import fails, check the message shown by **Import from Shopify** and retry when Shopify is available.

### Connection and import path

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Enter shop domain and app credentials] --> B[Save credentials in iOS Keychain]
  B --> C[Request Shopify access token]
  C --> D[Fetch shop and active locations]
  D --> E[Choose location for stock and orders]
  E --> F[Import variants collections customers and discounts]
  E --> G[Set up shared storage when using multiple registers]
```

pages.title: Theme, tiles and accent
pages.summary: Choose Light, Dark or System appearance, adjust tile size and pick an accent colour for this iPad.
pages.lead: Open **More ▸ Settings ▸ Theme** to change the app's appearance, Checkout tile size and accent colour on this iPad.

sections.basic:
### Choose an appearance
Select **Light**, **Dark** or **System**. **System** follows the iPad's appearance setting.

### Change tile size and accent
Choose **Small**, **Medium** or **Large** under **Tile size**. Tap an accent swatch to change the app's highlight colour; **Default** restores the standard dark accent.

The theme, tile size and accent update immediately and are stored on this register.
sections.deep:
### Appearance does not change the grid
Theme changes colours and the general appearance. Tile size changes how large Checkout tiles appear, not which items or categories are on the grid. To edit the grid itself, see [[sales/grid]].

These choices are local to this iPad. They do not change another register's theme.

pages.title: Staff and roles
pages.summary: Add team members, set unique PINs and roles, require sign-in, and manage each person's display settings and pass.
pages.lead: Use **More ▸ Staff** to add the people who use the register, choose their role and set whether the till asks them to sign in. Each person can also have a cashier pass and their own display mode.

sections.basic:
### Add a staff member
1. Tap **Add staff member**.
2. Enter their name and a unique PIN of **4–6 digits**.
3. Choose **Cashier**, **Manager** or **Owner**, then tap **Add**.

PINs must not be shared between staff members. The app stores each PIN as a salted hash and shares the staff list with your other registers.

### Require sign-in
Turn on **Require PIN to use the register** to show the sign-in screen when the register is locked. Add at least one staff member first. To sign in, enter the PIN or scan that person's cashier pass.

You can switch staff from the **Switch staff** sheet without locking the register first. The cart stays as it is. The register will not switch people while a card payment is in progress.

### Change or remove someone
Tap a person's row to open their settings. Choose their display mode, manage their cashier pass, or remove them. Removing someone makes their PIN and pass stop working.

For issuing, printing or cancelling a pass, see [[staff/passes]]. For the per-person screen layout, see [[staff/modes]].
sections.deep:
### What roles control
- **Cashier** accounts do not see **Reports**, **Staff** or **Settings** while staff sign-in is required.
- **Manager** and **Owner** accounts can see those More menu entries.
- Display modes can hide menu entries, but never add access that a role does not have.
- Without staff sign-in enabled, the till acts as the owner for role-gated functions.

The Staff screen also has role switches for who may set item, line and whole-order price adjustments. Owners cannot be restricted. Managers or owners can change those switches; a manager can do so when the team has no owner account.

### Staff settings are shared
PIN hashes, roles, passes and each person's display choice travel with the shared staff settings. A pass's scannable code is kept only on the iPad that issued it; other registers can recognise it from its hash but cannot reprint its code.
sections.advanced:
### Staff and sign-in flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD

  B --> C[Require PIN on register]
  C --> D[Sign in by PIN or cashier pass]

  E --> F[Share staff settings with other registers]
```

pages.title: Guided checkout
pages.summary: Take a sale through Items, Customer, Discount, Check and Pay, one question at a time.
pages.lead: Guided checkout gives the cashier one step at a time: **Items**, **Customer**, **Discount**, **Check** and **Pay**. It is used by **Minimal** mode and can be switched on for **Custom** mode.

sections.basic:
### Take a sale through the steps
1. **Items**: tap or scan the products. Add at least one item before pressing **Next**.
2. **Customer**: find or add a customer, or tap **No, carry on**.
3. **Discount**: deals are applied automatically. Add a voucher or special price if needed, or tap **No, carry on**.
4. **Check**: review the items and total with the customer. Tap an item to change or remove it, then tap **Looks right**.
5. **Pay**: tap **Take payment**. Choose card, cash, gift card or a mix on the usual payment screen.

The progress bar shows which step you are on. Use **Back** to return to an earlier step.

### More options
Tap **More options** at the top to add a custom amount, sell a gift card, check whether the drawer can make change, save or open a saved cart, or start again. Starting again clears the cart after confirmation.
sections.deep:
### The steps are prompts, not new sale rules
Guided checkout uses the same cart, prices, discounts, customer and payment flows as the regular Checkout screen. It does not change how a sale is calculated or recorded.

The Customer and Discount steps are optional. A new empty cart returns to **Items**. If a sale has already taken a part payment, the flow resumes at **Pay**; the part-paid sale cannot be edited until payment is finished.

### Checks before payment
The **Check** step shows the cart and any bundle combinations that need a customer check. If the cart has a price adjustment requiring confirmation, that review appears before the payment screen. The cashier still gets the deal even when a bundle is not a recommended pair.
sections.advanced:
### Flow
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Items add one or more] --> B[Customer optional]
  B --> C[Discount optional]
  C --> D[Check items prices and deals]
  D --> E[Review price adjustments if needed]
  E --> F[Pay on the normal payment screen]
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Guided screen and More options | `src/screens/GuidedCheckout.tsx` |
| Step order, progress and advance rules | `STEPS`, `canAdvance`, `settle` in `src/lib/guidedFlow.ts` |
| Select guided checkout for Minimal or Custom | `guided` in `src/lib/uiMode.ts`, `src/ui/uiProfile.tsx` |
| Guided screen navigation | `src/ui/nav.tsx` |
| Tests | `tests/guidedflow.test.ts` |

When a part payment exists, the cart is locked for editing and the guided flow settles directly on Pay so the cashier can finish the remaining balance.

pages.title: Display modes
pages.summary: Set Standard, Simple, Minimal or Custom mode for each staff member without changing what their role is allowed to do.
pages.lead: Each staff member has a display mode, set from their row in **More ▸ Staff**. It changes how the POS is arranged for them, not their role permissions.

sections.basic:
### Choose a mode
- **Standard** shows the full app in its usual layout.
- **Simple** keeps the same features, with larger text and plain-English explanations in the More menu.
- **Minimal** uses the largest text, fewer tabs and More entries, and asks one checkout question at a time.
- **Custom** lets you choose text size, tabs, More entries, explanations and guided checkout separately.

Tap the staff member's row in Staff, select a mode under **Display mode**, then close the sheet. Each person's choice follows their staff record to the other registers.

### Custom choices
In **Custom**, choose **Normal**, **Large** or **Extra large** text; turn plain-English lines under More entries on or off; choose which tabs and More entries to show; and turn **Guided steps** on or off.

See [[staff/guided-checkout]] for what happens in that flow.
sections.deep:
### Tabs and More entries
- **All** tabs shows Checkout, Inventory, Transactions, Notifications and More.
- **No alerts** removes only the Notifications tab.
- **Basic** shows Checkout, Transactions and More.
- **All** More entries means everything the person's role allows. **Everyday** adds Items and Customers to the essential entries. **Essentials** keeps Orders, Saved carts, Gift cards, Cash drawer, Support & diagnostics, Help and Lock register, subject to role access.

Cashiers do not get manager-only entries such as Reports, Staff and Settings when staff sign-in is required. A display mode cannot grant them those entries. Checkout and More stay available so the person can do their job and get back to other parts of the app.

### The sole-admin safeguard
If the only Manager or Owner selects a mode that hides Staff or Settings, the POS shows those entries anyway. This prevents the only administrator from losing the controls needed to change the mode back.

Changing to **Custom** starts from the mode the person was using, so its text size and menu choices carry over until you change them.
sections.advanced:
### Mode resolution
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Read the staff member display mode] --> B[Resolve text tabs More and guided choices]
  B --> C[Limit More entries by staff role]
  C --> D{Only manager or owner}
  D -->|yes| E[Keep Staff and Settings visible]
  D -->|no| F[Show the resolved menus]
```

pages.title: Cashier passes and signing in
pages.summary: Issue a cashier pass, print or share it, add it to Apple Wallet, and use it to sign in or switch staff.
pages.lead: A cashier pass is a scannable alternative to typing a staff member's PIN. Issue it from **More ▸ Staff**, then print it, save or share a PDF, or send it to Apple Wallet.

sections.basic:
### Issue and use a pass
1. In **More ▸ Staff**, tap the person and choose **Cashier pass**.
2. Tap **Issue pass**. Choose **QR code** or **Code 128** for a standard shop barcode scanner.
3. Print the pass, save/share the PDF, or send it to Apple Wallet.
4. On the sign-in screen or **Switch staff** sheet, scan the pass with a Bluetooth scanner. You can also tap **Scan pass** to use the camera.

Most Bluetooth scanners and the camera can read the QR code. Choose Code 128 if your scanner only reads standard shop barcodes. A PIN remains available as another way to sign in.

### Replace or cancel a pass
**Replace pass** creates a new code and immediately disables the old one. Any printed copy or Wallet pass with the old code must be replaced. **Cancel pass** disables it; the staff member can still sign in with their PIN.

### Apple Wallet
Sending to Apple Wallet needs the pass server link and secret configured in **Settings ▸ Gift cards**. The app creates the Wallet pass, then opens the iPad's share sheet so you can send it to the staff member's iPhone. They tap **Add** there.
sections.deep:
### If this iPad no longer has the code
The pass code is saved only on the iPad that issued it. The shared staff list contains a hash, which lets other registers verify scans but cannot recover or print the original code. If the issuing iPad has lost its saved copy, choose **Replace pass** on a register with the staff list; the old code will stop working and the new code can be printed or sent from that iPad.

Scanning a pass signs the person in or takes over from the currently signed-in staff member. The cart stays in place. Switching is blocked while a card payment is waiting on the reader; finish the payment first.
sections.advanced:
### Pass lifecycle
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Issue random pass code] --> B[Share salted code hash with staff settings]
  A --> C[Keep recoverable code on issuing iPad]
  C --> D[Print PDF or request Apple Wallet pass]
  E[Scan code] --> F[Match code against staff hash]
  G[Replace or cancel] --> H[Old code no longer matches]
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Issue, replace, cancel, print and share | `StaffPassSheet` in `src/screens/StaffPass.tsx` |
| Hash and match pass codes | `src/lib/badge.ts` |
| Keep the issuing iPad's copy | `src/lib/badgeStore.ts` |
| PIN/pass sign-in and switching | `src/lib/staffAuth.ts` |
| Camera and HID scanners | `CameraScanner`, `HidScanner` in `src/screens/Scanner.tsx` |
| Create an Apple Wallet pass | `requestStaffPass` in `src/lib/passUrl.ts` |

Wallet pass creation requires the separately configured pass server. Printing and PDF sharing use the iPad's print/share interfaces; those options do not require Wallet setup.

pages.title: Screensaver and keep-awake
pages.summary: Keep the iPad awake or show a branded idle screen, with a shorter wait when the register is logged out.
pages.lead: Open **More ▸ Settings ▸ Screensaver & display** to stop the iPad sleeping or show a logo screen when the register is idle. These choices are for this iPad, not a staff member's display mode.

sections.basic:
### Keep the iPad awake
Turn on **Keep iPad awake** to stop iOS from auto-locking or dimming while the POS is open. This is separate from the Screensaver switch. The app recommends leaving it on for a till and keeping the iPad plugged in.

### Show an idle screen
Turn on **Screensaver**, then choose **Show after** 1, 2, 5, 10 or 30 minutes. It shows a logo on a background colour; if there is no usable logo, it shows the shop name or **Point of sale**.

Tap the screen once to wake it. If the register was locked, waking the screen does not sign anyone in; use the PIN or cashier pass on the sign-in screen.

### Set a logo
Use **Logo link (https)** for a secure image URL, or tap **Upload an image from Files…**. PNG and JPG are supported; SVG files are not. An uploaded logo is stored on this iPad. You can choose a background swatch or enter a three- or six-digit hex colour, then tap **Preview full screen**.
sections.deep:
### Logged-out timing and other options
- **Show when logged out** uses a shorter wait on the PIN screen. Choose **Logged-out wait** of 5, 15, 30 or 60 seconds.
- **Slowly move the logo** drifts the image around the screen. **Show the time** adds a clock.
- When the register is logged out and the shorter wait is enabled, the screensaver uses the shorter of the logged-out wait and normal idle time.
- It never covers the screen while a card payment is waiting on the reader.

The idle timer resets when someone touches the app, types or scans. The screensaver and Keep iPad awake settings belong to this device; they do not follow the staff member to another register.
sections.advanced:
### Idle screen rules
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Check screensaver enabled and time idle] --> B{Card payment waiting}
  B -->|yes| C[Keep the POS visible]
  B -->|no| D{Logged out and short wait enabled}
  D -->|yes| E[Use shorter of waits]
  D -->|no| F[Use normal idle wait]
  E --> G[Show screensaver when wait is reached]
  F --> G
```

pages.title: Help home
pages.summary: How to find things in this help, and what Basic, Deep and Advanced mean.
pages.lead: This help explains every part of the POS: what each screen is for, how to do each job, what the messages mean, and what to do when something goes wrong.

sections.basic:
### Finding what you need
- Open the **Help** screen (More ▸ Help). Pages are grouped by job: selling, taking payment, the cash drawer, gift cards, orders and refunds, stock, staff, settings, and fixing problems.
- Tap the **?** in a screen header to open help for that screen. Some error alerts also have a **Help** button that opens the relevant troubleshooting page.
- Use the search box at the top. Type a word or two ("refund", "card declined") and every word has to match.
- A page ends with **Related pages**. Words in blue take you to another page.
- For troubleshooting, start at [[fix]]. For the rules behind data, staff access and money, see [[concepts]].

### Choosing how much detail you want
Every page has up to three levels. You pick one and the Help screen remembers it.

| Level | What you get |
|---|---|
| **Basic** | What you need to know to do the job. Start here. |
| **Deep** | Basic, plus a plain-English look at how it works, so the odd behaviours make sense. |
| **Advanced** | Everything above, plus the code behind it, flowcharts, and how to trace a fault that the screen cannot fix. |

A deeper level always includes the levels above it, so you never have to read two copies of a page.

### If a page is missing or wrong
Tell the person who looks after the POS. The pages are ordinary text files, so a fix is a small edit and shows up everywhere (the app and the website) at once.
sections.deep:
### One set of pages, two places to read them
The pages are Markdown files kept in one folder. The app has a copy built in, so it works with no internet, and the docs website serves the same files. Because both read the same source, they cannot drift apart. When a page changes, its fingerprint (a short code) changes too, so a device can tell whether it has the latest.

### How pages are organised
Each page has a **parent**, which makes the folders-inside-folders shape you see on the Help screen. Pages also point at each other with links, and each page shows the pages that link to it. Nothing is listed by hand: the contents list is built from the parents, so a new page appears in the right place the moment it exists.

### Checks before a page is accepted
A page cannot be added to the set unless its links all go somewhere, its parent exists, it has a Basic section, and its code blocks are closed. This is why you should not meet a dead link while reading.
sections.advanced:
### Where things live
| What | Where |
|---|---|
| The pages | `help/**/*.md` (a page is `help/<folder>/<name>.md`; a folder's own page is `index.md`) |
| Format, parsing, checks, search | `src/lib/helpDocs.ts` (pure, no React) |
| Build and check script | `scripts/build-help.ts` (`npm run help:build`, `npm run help:check`) |
| What the app and the website read | `help/help.json` (generated, do not edit by hand) |
| Tests | `tests/helpdocs.test.ts` |
| Notes for people writing pages | `help/README.md` |

### The page format
A page is a header, an optional lead, and up to three sections:

```text
---
id: sales/cart-and-prices
title: The cart and how prices are worked out
parent: sales
summary: One line for lists and search.
tags: [cart, discount]
related: [pay]
updated: 2026-10-11
---
Lead text, shown at every depth.
## Basic
## Deep
## Advanced
```

Rules the checker enforces (`validatePages`): the `id` must match the file path (`sales/index.md` is `sales`, `start.md` is `start`); every page except `start` has a `parent` that exists, with no loops; every `[[link]]` and every `related` entry must point at a real page; `## Basic` must be present; code fences must close; and `##` is reserved for the three depth headings, so inside a section you use `###`.

### How the pieces fit
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[help/*.md] -->|parsePage| B[Page objects]
  B -->|validatePages| C{Any problems?}
  C -->|yes| D[build stops, lists each problem]
  C -->|no| E[makeBundle]
  E --> F[help/help.json]
  F --> G[App: built-in copy]
  F --> H[Docs website]
```

### Showing a page at a depth
`selectDepth(page, depth)` returns the lead, then each section down to the chosen depth. `resolveLinks` turns `[[id|text]]` into a real link for whichever viewer is showing it, and leaves plain text if the id is unknown, so raw brackets never reach the screen. `searchPages` requires every word to match and ranks title and tag matches above body matches. `buildIndex` gives the parent/child tree and the "pages that link here" lists; `trail` gives the path from the top page down to a page.

### Tracing a problem
- A page is not showing up: run `npm run help:check`. It prints every problem with the file name.
- The app shows an old page: compare `version` in `help/help.json` with the one the app holds (`readBundle` rejects a bundle it cannot use, and the app then keeps its built-in copy).
- A link is plain text instead of a link: the id in `[[...]]` does not exist, so `resolveLinks` printed only its text. The checker would have refused it, so look for a page that was deleted or renamed after the link was written.

pages.title: Items and inventory
pages.summary: Find and edit catalogue items, inspect stock, and choose where to count or adjust inventory.
pages.lead: Shopify is the shared product catalogue. **Items** is for finding and editing product details; **Inventory** is for checking and changing stock counts.

sections.basic:
### Choose the right screen
- Open **More ▸ Items** to search products and variations, change price, SKU, barcode or cost, or create an item.
- Open the **Inventory** tab to see stock, filter the catalogue, and receive, adjust or count quantities.
- A product can have several variations. Each variation has its own price, SKU, barcode and stock count.

For stock words and what happens when sales or refunds change a count, see [[sales/variants-and-stock]]. For Inventory filters, grouping and stock updates, see [[stock/inventory]]. For catalogue editing and creating an item, see [[stock/items]].

### If an item is missing
Import or refresh from Shopify in **More ▸ Settings ▸ Shopify**. Inventory can include active, draft and archived products, but its default status filter is **Active**. Use Filters to include other statuses. When counts still differ, use **Refresh stock from Shopify** in Inventory.
sections.deep:
### Products and variations
A Shopify product may contain one or more variants. The Items list has one row for each variant, even when product names repeat. Inventory can show every variant as a flat list or group variants under a product. Changing an item's price or identifiers in this POS saves to Shopify; stock counts are changed from Inventory.

### What is stored locally
The app imports product/variant details and the selected location's available stock into its local catalogue. It refreshes the catalogue from Shopify on request and receives shared stock changes while open. Each register updates its own local view, while Shopify remains the shared source.
sections.advanced:
### Catalogue and stock flow
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Import catalogue from Shopify] --> B[Store products and variants locally]
  B --> C[Items searches and edits product details]
  B --> D[Inventory filters variants and updates stock]
  D --> E[Send stock mutation to Shopify]
  E --> F[Other registers refresh their local view]
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Catalogue type | `Variant` in `src/lib/types.ts` |
| Bulk catalogue import | `fetchVariants`, `fetchCollections` in `src/lib/shopify/catalogue.ts` |
| Items list and editor | `ItemsList`, `EditItem` in `src/screens/Items.tsx` |
| Inventory list and count UI | `src/screens/Inventory.tsx` |
| Stock updates | `setStock`, `adjustStock` in `src/lib/shopify/inventory.ts` |
| Search, filters and grouping | `src/lib/inventoryView.ts` |

`Variant.stock` is a number when tracked and `null` when not tracked. A negative number means Shopify has recorded more sales than available stock, not that the value is missing.

pages.title: The Inventory screen
pages.summary: Search and filter the product catalogue, group variations, and receive, adjust or count stock.
pages.lead: The **Inventory** tab shows stock for the catalogue on this iPad. Search or filter to find a variation, then tap it to receive stock, make an adjustment, or set a counted quantity.

sections.basic:
### Find an item
Search by product name, variation, SKU or barcode. Use the quick chips for **All**, **Low**, **Out (0)** and **Negative**. **Filters** opens the full options:
- **Category**: all categories or one Shopify collection.
- **Stock level**: All, Low, Out (0), Negative, Tracked or Not tracked.
- **Low** threshold: choose 1, 2, 3, 5 or 10 when Low is selected.
- **Product status**: Active, Draft, Archived or All.
- **Sort by**: name, stock low/high first, price low/high first, or recently updated.
- **Show variations**: each variant on its own, or **Nested under item**.

The header shows matching variant and product counts. In nested view, tap a product row to expand or collapse its variations. Searching expands matching groups automatically.

### Change a stock count
Tap a variant row. Choose:
- **Receive** to add the quantity that arrived.
- **Adjust** to add or remove stock. Choose Add/Remove and a reason such as correction, damaged or shrinkage.
- **Count** to enter the actual quantity you counted; this replaces the old number.

Enter a whole number and tap **Apply** or **Set stock to …**. The POS sends the change to Shopify and updates this register's catalogue after success. A missing inventory link or location prevents the update; choose a Shopify location or import the item again.

### Refresh and saved choices
Tap **Refresh stock from Shopify** at the bottom to import the catalogue again. The Filters sheet shows the total variants on this device and the last import time, so you can compare it with Shopify. Filter, sort, grouping and low-threshold preferences are remembered on this iPad.
sections.deep:
### What the filters mean
- **Low** includes tracked counts from zero through the chosen threshold.
- **Out (0)** means exactly zero. **Negative** means less than zero.
- **Tracked** includes any count, including negative. **Not tracked** has no count and is not the same as zero.
- A category filter uses the selected Shopify collection. Products can appear in more than one collection.
- By default the screen filters to **Active** products. Draft and archived variants remain in the local catalogue, but are hidden until the status is changed.

The app's default low threshold is 2 and default sort is Stock: low first. Changing to nested or flat view does not change the underlying stock.

### Product groups
Nested groups show a product title, variation count, combined tracked stock and price range. A product with one variant stays a plain row. Untracked variants do not add a numeric stock; a group with no tracked variants shows a dash. The group total can be negative if its tracked variants sum below zero.

### If the catalogue count is lower than Shopify
Tap **Refresh stock from Shopify** and compare the total variant count and import time shown in Filters. The catalogue import uses Shopify's bulk product-variant query and the selected location. Draft and archived status filters can hide rows, but the device total in the Filters sheet counts the entire local catalogue.

If the same variant still differs from Shopify, check the selected location, tracked setting and **available** quantity in [[fix/stock-mismatch]].
sections.advanced:
### Stock update path
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Choose variant and Receive Adjust or Count] --> B{Inventory item and location available}
  B -->|no| C[Show Not linked message]
  B -->|yes| D[Send inventory mutation to Shopify]
  D -->|success| E[Update local variant count]
  D -->|failure| F[Show connection or stock error]
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Inventory list, sheets and refresh | `src/screens/Inventory.tsx` |
| Filter, sort, grouping and rows | `filterVariants`, `sortVariants`, `groupVariants`, `buildRows` in `src/lib/inventoryView.ts` |
| Set exact count | `setStock` in `src/lib/shopify/inventory.ts` |
| Receive or adjust | `adjustStock` in `src/lib/shopify/inventory.ts` |
| Saved Inventory preferences | `inventory` in `src/state/store.ts` |
| Tests | `tests/inventory.test.ts` |

The filter/search is applied before grouping. The list has no fixed row cap. In stock-ascending or stock-descending order, untracked variants always sort last. When grouped, group ordering uses total tracked stock, the lowest price, or latest update, depending on the selected sort.

pages.title: Items and creating one
pages.summary: Search the catalogue, edit a variant's price and identifiers, or create a tracked product in Shopify.
pages.lead: The **Items** screen is the catalogue editor. It lists variants and lets you change a variant's price, SKU, barcode and cost, or create a new product.

sections.basic:
### Find or edit a variant
Open **More ▸ Items** and search by product name, variant, SKU or barcode. Tap a row to edit it. Change **Price**, **SKU**, **Barcode** or **Cost**, then tap **Save to Shopify**. Cost is used for profit reporting. Use **Inventory** to receive stock, adjust it or enter a stock count: [[stock/inventory]].

### Create an item
1. In Items, tap **+** and choose a name and price. Both are required.
2. Add a SKU, barcode and cost if you use them.
3. If offered, enter **Starting stock** and choose a category.
4. Tap **Create item**. The app needs a Shopify location and an internet connection.

The new product is created in Shopify, then the app imports the catalogue again. New products are tracked at the selected location. If the create step reports an error, check Shopify and refresh before trying again.

### Price, SKU and barcode
Each variation has its own price and identifiers. A product with multiple variations appears as multiple rows with the same product name. Changing a variant's details does not rename the Shopify product; use Shopify admin for product titles and variant options.
sections.deep:
### What the create form writes
The form creates an active Shopify product with its default variant, then sets the variant's price, barcode, SKU, cost and inventory tracking. It activates inventory at the selected location and can add the product to one chosen Shopify collection. The app refreshes its local catalogue after creation.

### A known starting-stock issue
The form currently displays **Starting stock**, but the create request does not apply the entered quantity after inventory is activated. New stock therefore needs to be set from **Inventory** after creation. This is recorded as an open follow-up in `docs/PROGRESS.md`; do not rely on the form's Starting stock field until that is fixed.
sections.advanced:
### Create and edit path
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Enter product details] --> B[Create active product in Shopify]
  B --> C[Set default variant price and identifiers]
  C --> D[Activate tracked inventory at selected location]
  D --> E[Add product to optional collection]
  E --> F[Refresh local catalogue]
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Items list, create and edit forms | `ItemsList`, `CreateItem`, `EditItem` in `src/screens/Items.tsx` |
| Shopify product and variant writes | `createItem`, `updateVariant` in `src/lib/shopify/products.ts` |
| Catalogue refresh after creation | `importFromShopify` in `src/lib/sync.ts` |
| Stock changes | `src/screens/Inventory.tsx`, `src/lib/shopify/inventory.ts` |

`createItem` creates an active product and its default variant, then enables tracked inventory at the selected location. Although the form input type has an optional `stock` field, the current helper does not send that quantity to Shopify.
